articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्षको बहारः ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बाग्मती प्रदेशको राजधानी हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ लाई लक्षित गर्दै ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइन लागिएको पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अन्तर्गत सरसफाइ थालिएको हो ।

यो वर्ष बाग्मतीको प्रादेशिक राजधानीस्थित हेटौँडा उपमहानगरपालिकाले पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मनाउँदैछ । पर्यटन वर्षको कार्यक्रम अन्तर्गत सून्य फोहोर अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । यहि अभियान अन्तर्गत शनिवार हातमा कुचो र बोरा बोकेर जनप्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षाकर्मी, टोल विकास संस्थाका पदाधिकारी र स्थानीयवासी सडकमा निस्किए । हेटौँडाका सडकदेखि टोलसम्म सरसफाइ गर्दै उनीहरूले ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियान शुरु गरेका हुन् ।

फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई केवल सरसफाइ अभियानका रूपमा नभई पर्यटन, वातावरण संरक्षण र नागरिक संस्कृतिसँग जोडिएको दीर्घकालीन अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइने योजना उपमहानगरपालिकाको छ । उपमहानगरपालिकाले ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइने पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अघि सारिएको हो ।

मुख्य तथा सहायक सडक, सार्वजनिक स्थल र पर्यटकीय क्षेत्रको सरसफाइसँगै वृक्षारोपण र सौन्दर्यीकरणलाई पनि अभियानको प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ । टोल विकास संस्था नगर समन्वय समितिको संयोजनमा सुरु भएको अभियान नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोल विकास संस्थामा सुरु गरिएको छ । पर्यटन वर्षको अवसरमा सुरु गरिएको ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियानले नगरको स्वच्छता र सौन्दर्य कायम राख्दै हेटौँडालाई पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यका रूपमा चिनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको दाबी छ ।

पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मा हेटौँडामा आन्तरिक तथा बाह्य पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउने उपमहानगरपालिकाको लक्ष्य छ । पर्यटकलाई आकर्षित गर्न नयाँ गन्तव्यको प्रचारसँगै शहरको स्वच्छता, सौन्दर्य र व्यवस्थित वातावरणलाई पनि प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ ।

यही उद्देश्यले सुरु गरिएको यो अभियानलाई नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोलसम्म विस्तार गरिँदैछ । टोल–टोलमा सरसफाइ र फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउँदै हेटौँडालाई स्वच्छ, सुन्दर र पर्यटकमैत्री शहरका रूपमा विकास गर्ने र पर्यटन वर्षमा बढीभन्दा बढी पर्यटक भित्र्याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

articles.title: इन्सेन्टिभ वितरण नहुँदा सेवा ठप्प, मर्कामा सर्वसाधारण विरामी
articles.summary:
महोत्तरी । प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा सेवा लिन आउने नागरिक अनाहकमा पिडित बन्न पुगेका छन । मेडिकल सुपिरिटेंडेन्ट, अस्पताल संचालन तथा व्यस्थापन् समिति अध्यक्ष बिचको तालमेल समस्या र भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको बाकी इन्सेन्टिभ जस्ता आन्तरिक विवादका कारण सेवाग्राहीलाई मर्का परिरहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा अस्पतालमा भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा बन्द भएपछि बिरामीहरू निजी स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा महँगो शुल्क तिरेर सेवा लिन बाध्य छन् । अस्पताल प्रशासनले प्राविधिक कारणले सेवा वन्द रहेको सूचना टॉस गरि सेवा अवरुद्ध रहेको बताएको छ । तर भित्री कुरा भने भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने चिकित्सकलाई इन्सेन्टिभ उपलब्ध नगराइएका कारण सो सेवा विगत दुई हप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि वन्द रहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवले इन्सेन्टिभकै समस्याको कारणले दुईहप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा सुचारू हुन नसकेको स्विकारे । आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\०८३ मा चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएका कारण सेवा वन्द गरेको बताउदै समस्या समाधानको पहल गरिरहेको निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवको भनाइ छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका अस्पताल सञ्चालन तथा व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष रोहित प्रसाद ठाकुरले पनि काम गर्ने चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएकै कारणले सेवा अवरुद्ध भएको बताए । उनले सेवा सुचारुको पहल गरिरहेको बताउदै अस्पताल व्यवस्थापन समितिको जेठ २८ गते बसेको बैठकले इन्सेन्टिभ दिने निर्णय गरेपनि सो किन वितरण गरिएन ? आशंका छन् ।

स्वास्थ सेवा जस्तो संवेदनशील संस्थाले अस्पतालको आन्तरिक तथा प्रशासनिक समस्याकै कारण सेवा ठप्प पार्नु, आम नागरिकलाई अनाहकमा समस्या दिनु स्वभाविक रुपमा लिन सकिदैन्। तर, यसको समाधान कसरी होला? सर्वसाधारणले नै सोध्न थालेका छन् ।

articles.title: देश धान्ने क्षेत्रमै संकट, श्रमिक विदेश पठाउन बन्द !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । वैदेशिक रोजगारीबाट आउने रेमिट्यान्सले देशको अर्थतन्त्र धान्न सहयोग पु¥याइरहेका म्यानपावर व्यवसायीले सरकारविरुद्ध दबाब बढाएका छन् । १५ बुँदे माग अघि सार्दै नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले शुक्रवारदेखि वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ । व्यवसायीहरूले नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म कामदार नपठाउने अडान लिएका छन् ।

नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार क्षेत्रका नीतिगत समस्या समाधान नभएको भन्दै शुक्रवारदेखि श्रमिक विदेश पठाउने कार्य पूर्ण रूपमा स्थगित गरेको छ । काठमाडौँमा पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै संघले रेमिट्यान्सले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा ठूलो योगदान पु¥याए पनि सरकारले समयानुकूल नीति सुधार नगर्दा व्यवसायी र श्रमिक दुवै प्रभावित भएको जनाएको छ ।

संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार ऐन–२०६४ लाई समयसापेक्ष संशोधन, पारदर्शी लागत निर्धारण, वैज्ञानिक सेवा शुल्क, श्रमिक लक्षित गन्तव्य मुलुकको हवाई भाडा घटाउने तथा कृत्रिम अभाव अन्त्य गर्न माग गरेको छ । युरोपका नयाँ श्रम बजार, दक्षिण कोरियाको ई–सेभेन भिसा, जापानको ईएसडी कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन, महिला घरेलु कामदारका लागि नयाँ गन्तव्य खुला गर्ने र विभिन्न मुलुकमा देखिएका प्रशासनिक तथा बिचौलिया समस्या कूटनीतिक पहलमार्फत समाधान गर्नुपर्ने माग पनि अघि सारिएको छ ।

संघले मागपत्र प्रमाणीकरण र श्रम स्वीकृतिलाई पूर्ण रूपमा स्वचालित बनाउन, ५ हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली श्रमिक रहेका मुलुकमा श्रम सहचारी तथा काउन्सिलर नियुक्त गर्न, व्यवसायीले राखेको धरौटीको ब्याज उपलब्ध गराउन र श्रमिकलाई बिना धितो सहुलियतपूर्ण कर्जा दिने व्यवस्था गर्न पनि सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ । अध्यक्ष खत्रीले विशेष परिस्थितिमा सरकारकै निर्णय कार्यान्वयन गर्दा व्यवसायीमाथि कारबाही गरिएको आरोप लगाउँदै अब नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म श्रमिक नपठाउने स्पष्ट चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

संघले आफ्ना सबै माग सम्बोधन नभएसम्म शून्य समय घोषणा गर्दै वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द रहने जनाएको छ । व्यवसायीहरूको यो निर्णयले वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान तयारी गरिरहेका हजारौं नेपाली श्रमिक प्रत्यक्ष प्रभावित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: सेती नदि थुनिएर ताल बन्यो, स्थानीय जाग्राम बस्न बाध्य
articles.summary:
कास्की । केहि दिन यताको निरन्तर वर्षाले पोखराको रामघाटमा सेती नदी थुनिएर विशाल ताल बनेको छ । जसका कारण नदिसँगै जोडिएका सुकुम्बासी बस्ती बाढीले बगाउने जोखिममा रहेका छन् ।

सेती नदीलाई लिएर पोखराको भौगोलिक बनावट अत्यन्त जोखिममा रहेको चर्चा गरिन्छ , तर सेतिले निम्त्याएको जोखिम न्यून गर्न भने कुनै निकायको ध्यान पुग्न सकेको छैन । झट्ट हेर्दा यो दृश्य कुनै तालको होला भन्ने लाग्न सक्छ, तर नझुक्किनुस् यो कुनै ताल भने होइन ।

केहीदिन यता निरन्तर परेको वर्षको कारण सेती नदीमा पानीको बहाव निकै उच्च छ । हो पोखरा रामघाटमा फराकिलो रहेको सेती नदीको निकास सानो हुँदा पानी जान नसकेर विशाल ताल नै बनेको छ । सेती नदी थुनिएर ताल बन्दा अहिलेसम्म क्षति त भएको छैन तर संभावित क्षतिको जोखिम भने निकै बढेको छ ।

दाह संस्कारका लागि बनाइएका घाटहरु पुरै जलमग्न बनेका छन् । सेती किनारसँगै दुई दर्जन बढी सुकुम्बासी बस्ती छ, बर्खा लागे पछि कतिबेला बाढीले बगाउने हो भनेर जाग्राम बस्नु पर्ने अवस्था छ । अहिले ३ वर्ष यताकै ठूलो र डरलाग्दो तरिकाले सेती बढेको स्थानीय बताउँछन् ।

सेती नदी पोखराको अधिकांस भागमा भूमिगत भएर बगेको छ । पोखराको बीच भाग अर्थात् रामघाटमा भने सेती सतहमा देखिन्छ । यस आसपासको क्षेत्र अत्यन्त जोखिममा रहेपनि सुकुम्बासीका नाममा बस्ती बस्ने क्रम भने नरोकिदो जोखिम झनै बढ्दैछ । पछिल्लो समय झनझन गहिरिदै गएको सेती खोंच र निरन्तरको बर्षाका कारण कतिबेला ठूलो दुर्घटना निम्तिने भन्ने इतिहासविद्को चिन्ता छ ।

पोखराको भू–बनोट र निरन्तर वर्षाले भासिन सक्ने सम्भाव्यताले पोखरालाई वर्षेनी जोखिम तर्फ धकेलेको भूगोलविद्को बुझाई छ । नदी थुनिएर आफ्नो गतिमा जान नपाउँदा निरन्तर जमिनलाई खियाउनाले जोखिम बढेको भूगोलविद् कृष्ण प्रसाद पौडेल बताउँछन् ।

पोखराको भू–बनोट, बेलाबेलामा भएका जमीन भासिने घटना र भूमिगतरूपमा बगेको सेतीका कारण पोखराको जोखिमबारे बेलाबेला चर्चा हुने गर्दछ, तर त्यो चर्चालाई दीर्घकालीन समाधानको बाटोतर्फ भने कुनै निकायले लैजान सकेका छैनन् ।

articles.title: स्तनपान प्रवद्र्धनमा जोड, दोलखामा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना
articles.summary:
दोलखा । जीवनको दिगो सुरुवातका लागि स्तनपान प्रभावकारी कार्यहरूको सुदृढीकरण“ भन्ने नारासहित दोलखाको भीमेश्वर नगरपालिका–५ स्थित माटी स्वास्थ्य चौकीमा विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताह–२०२६ मनाइएको छ । कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमाहरूलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पोषण सामग्री वितरण तथा महिला स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविकालाई प्रोत्साहन गरिएको छ ।

विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताह–२०२६ को अवसरमा दोलखामा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा धुलिखेल अस्पताल दोलखाका विशेषज्ञ चिकित्सकहरूले गर्भवती महिलाको स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण, अल्ट्रासाउन्ड, स्वास्थ्य परामर्श तथा स्तनपान र शिशु पोषणबारे अभिमुखीकरण गरेका छन् ।

कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमालाई पोषण सामग्री, ब्ल्यांकेट तथा महिला स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविका र माटी स्वास्थ्य चौकीका स्वास्थ्यकर्मीलाई छाता वितरण गरिएको छ । ती सामग्री पूर्व स्वास्थ्य चौकी प्रमुख रामकृष्ण मास्केको पहलमा विभिन्न दाताबाट संकलन गरिएको हो ।

कार्यक्रममा जिल्लाको स्वास्थ्य अवस्था, शिशु स्वास्थ्यमा आमाको दूधको महत्व र स्तनपान प्रवद्र्धन अभियानबारे जानकारी गराइएको छ । समुदायस्तरमा यस्ता कार्यक्रमलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिइएको छ ।

भीमेश्वर नगरपालिकाले मातृ तथा शिशु स्वास्थ्यलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै स्वास्थ्य संस्थासँगको सहकार्यलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउने जनाएको छ ।

नेपाल क्षयरोग निवारण संस्थाले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिका कार्यक्रमलाई निरन्तरता दिइने जनाएको छ ।

कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमाहरूलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पोषण सामग्री वितरण तथा स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविका र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीलाई सम्मान गर्दै स्तनपानको महत्व समुदायसम्म पु¥याउने प्रयास गरिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: भूपेन्द्रसहित बैंकका उच्च अधिकारीमाथि छानबिन शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकमको अर्बौं मूल्य बराबरको पूर्वाधार बिक्री प्रकरणले नेपालको दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रमा ल्याएको तरंगको पराकम्प अझै कम भएको छैन । लाइसेन्स रद्द भएपछि राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने सम्पत्ति चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँमा बिक्री भएको विषय अहिले अनुसन्धानको केन्द्रमा छ ।

सीआईबीले पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीसहित बैंकका उच्च अधिकारीमाथि छानबिन अघि बढाएको छ । नेपालको दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्र एउटा प्रश्नले अझै तरंगित छ । राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने स्मार्ट टेलिकमको अर्बौं रुपैयाँ बराबरको सम्पत्ति कसरी निजी हातमा पुग्यो ? यसको जवाफ अझै मिल्न सकेको छैन । नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो अर्थात् सीआईबीले यही प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीलाई पक्राउ गरी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाइरहेको छ ।

काठमाडौं जिल्ला अदालतले भण्डारीमाथि थप अनुसन्धानका लागि प्रहरीलाई ६ दिनको म्याद दिएको छ । उनीमाथि ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात र संगठित अपराधसम्बन्धी कसुरमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ ।

स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० सालमा आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालनको अनुमति पाएको थियो । तर कम्पनीले नवीकरण दस्तुर र रोयल्टीबापतको करिब ३० अर्ब रुपैयाँ सरकारलाई बुझाउन सकेन । त्यसपछि २०८० वैशाख ३ गते यसको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भयो ।

कानुनअनुसार लाइसेन्स रद्द भएको दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीको टावर, नेटवर्क, उपकरण र अन्य पूर्वाधार राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ । तर सीआईबीको आरोप छः राज्यको नाममा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकले गैरकानुनी रूपमा लिलामी ग¥यो र त्यो सम्पत्ति एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले खरिद ग¥यो । स्मार्टको लिलामी मूल्य थियो चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार यो प्रक्रियामा तत्कालीन दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण अध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीको भूमिका सबैभन्दा बढि शंकास्पद देखिएको छ । यही अनुसन्धानका क्रममा नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकका अध्यक्ष पृथ्वीबहादुर पाण्डेसहित ६ जना सञ्चालकको बैंक खाता रोक्का गरिएको छ । प्रहरीले उनीहरूविरुद्ध पक्राउ पुर्जीसमेत लिएको बताइएको छ ।

खाता रोक्का भएका व्यक्तिमा अध्यक्ष पाण्डेसँगै प्रणय राजभण्डारी, दीपांकर शाक्य, कविकुमार तिव्रेवाला, शालिकराम बेलवासे र शोभा श्रेष्ठ रहेका छन् ।

अर्का सञ्चालक मदनकुमार आचार्यले भने सीआईबीमा उपस्थित भएर बयान दिइसकेका कारण पक्राउ पुर्जीबाट बाहिर रहेको बुझिएको छ ।

फेरि एकपटक बिक्रि प्रक्रियाको कुरा गरौँ

स्मार्ट टेलिकमकोे सम्पत्ति बिक्री प्रक्रिया नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकले स्मार्ट टेलिकमले सम्पत्ति बिक्रिका लागि बोलपत्र आह्वान गरेसँगै अघि बढेको थियो । यसमा तीन कम्पनी सहभागी भए । ट्रान्सगेट टेकले ४४ करोड ५० लाख रुपैयाँ, प्रोफेसनल बिजनेस नेटवर्कले ४२ करोड ५० लाख रुपैयाँ र एनसेल आजियाटाले चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँको प्रस्ताव पेस ग¥यो ।

बैंकले सबैभन्दा बढी रकम प्रस्ताव गर्ने एनसेलको बोलपत्र स्वीकार ग¥यो । तर यी तीन कम्पनीले राखेको खरिद मूल्य प्रस्ताव नै शंकास्पद देखिन्छ । सेटिङमै तीन कम्पनी एकै व्यक्तिबाट परिचालित देखिन्छ । दुई कम्पनीको प्रस्तावभन्दा एनसेल आजियाटाको प्रस्ताव आकाश जमिन फरक छ ।

यो किनबेचमा बैंकको दाबी छ, उसले ऋण असुलीका लागि बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थासम्बन्धी ऐनको व्यवस्थाअनुसार धितो बिक्री गरेको हो । तर जुन सम्पत्ति राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको थियो, त्यसलाई बैंकले बिक्री गर्ने अधिकार कसरी पायो भन्ने सीआईबीको प्रश्न छ ।

यसअघि सीआईबीले स्मार्ट टेलिकमका सञ्चालक सर्वेश जोशी र नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत ज्योति प्रकाश पाण्डेलाई पनि पक्राउ गरी अनुसन्धान गरेको थियो । सीआईबीले केही महिनादेखि यो प्रकरणमाथि अध्ययन अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

तत्कालिन मन्त्री शर्माको भूमिका !

भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बन्नुअघि तत्कालिन सञ्चारमन्त्री रेखा शर्माका सल्लाहकार थिए । शर्माको जोडबलमा भण्डारीलाई प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्षमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल ‘प्रचण्ड’ नेतृत्वको सरकारले नियुक्त गरेको थियो । प्राधिकरण अध्यक्ष बन्नुअघि भण्डारी इन्टरग्रुप टेलिकम एसएल लिमिटेड र स्मार्ट मोबाइल बुरुन्डीको प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत भइसकेका व्यक्ति हुन् ।

उनले मरु डिजिटल वालेट चलाउने कम्पनी पेनेपमा अध्यक्षका रुपमा ५ वर्ष १० महिना काम गरेका थिए । कार्यकाल ७ महिना बाँकी छँदै प्राधिकरणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनालले तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्ड र तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री शर्माको दबाब खेप्न नसकेपछि २०८० पुस २४ गते राजीनामा दिएपछि भण्डारी दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रको नियामक प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

वर्तमान सरकारले सार्वजनिक पदाधिकारीसम्बन्धी विशेष व्यवस्थाअन्तर्गत भण्डारीलाई पदबाट बर्खास्त गरेको हो । आलोचकहरूले भण्डारीको कार्यकालमा दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रका समस्या थप बढेको आरोप लगाएका छन् । स्मार्ट टेलिकमका टावर राख्न दिएका दुई सयभन्दा बढी घरधनीले समेत लामो समयदेखि भाडा नपाएको गुनासो गर्दै आएका छन् ।

सीआईबीको अनुसन्धानले राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनु पर्ने अर्बौ मूल्यको दूरसञ्चार पूर्वाधार कानूनी प्रक्रियाबाट बिक्रि भएको थियो कि मिलेमतोमा भन्ने प्रश्नको उत्तर खोजिरहेको छ । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणको अन्तिम निष्कर्ष अनुसन्धान र अदालतको प्रक्रियाले तय गर्नेछ ।

articles.title: टुसा व्यापारमा कडाई, पोखरामा माग भन्दा कम आपूर्ति
articles.summary:
कास्की । साउन लागेसँगै पोखराको बजारमा पहाडी क्षेत्रमा पाइने औषधीय गुणयुक्त टुसाको कारोबार सुरु भएको छ । पोखरा घुम्न आउने पर्यटकका लागि टुसा लोकप्रिय कोसेली बन्दै गए पनि यस वर्ष उत्पादन र आपूर्ति घट्दा व्यापार पनि सुस्त बनेको छ ।

अन्नपूर्ण संरक्षण क्षेत्र आयोजनाले चोरी निकासी नियन्त्रण गरेसँगै बजारमा टुसाको उपलब्धता कम भएको जनाएको छ । पोखरा घुम्न आउने धेरैजसो आन्तरिक पर्यटक फर्किने बेला स्थानीय कोसेलीका रूपमा टुसा लैजान रुचाउँछन् ।

औषधीय गुणले भरिपूर्ण मानिने टुसाको तरकारी पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा झन् लोकप्रिय बन्दै गएको छ । अधिकांश टुसा पाइने क्षेत्र अन्नपूर्ण संरक्षण क्षेत्र आयोजना (एक्याप) अन्तर्गत पर्छन् । संरक्षणसँगै स्थानीयको आयआर्जनलाई समेत ध्यानमा राख्दै एक्यापले हरेक वर्ष साउन महिनाभर सर्वसाधारणलाई टुसा संकलन गर्न अनुमति दिने गरेको छ ।

असारदेखि भदौसम्म टुसा पलाउने मुख्य याम हो । कास्कीका ल्वाङ, घलेल, भुर्जुङखोला, सिक्लेस, ताङतिङ, याङजाकोट, घान्द्रुक, लान्द्रुक, धम्पुस र लुम्लेलगायत उच्च पहाडी क्षेत्रबाट बजारमा टुसा ल्याइन्छ । मानव स्वास्थ्यका लागि उपयोगी भएकाले यसको महत्व हरेक वर्ष बढ्दै गएको एक्यापको भनाइ छ ।

साउन महिनामा धेरैले माछामासु कम खाने परम्परा र यही समयमा टुसाको उत्पादन बढी हुने भएकाले व्यापार पनि बढ्ने गरेको थियो । तर यस वर्ष भने बजारको अवस्था फरक देखिएको छ । व्यापारीका अनुसार उत्पादन कम भएकाले बजारमा टुसाको आपूर्ति घटेको छ ।

अहिले पोखरामा प्रतिमुठा ८० देखि १५० रुपैयाँसम्ममा बिक्री भइरहेको छ । राम्रो व्यापार भएका दिन एकै स्थानबाट दुई सय मुठासम्म बिक्री हुने गरे पनि अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा यसपालि कारोबार घटेको व्यवसायीको भनाइ छ ।

पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा टुसाको चोरी निकासी बढेपछि एक्यापले व्यवस्थापन कडा बनाएको छ । बोलकबोल प्रक्रियामार्फत वैधानिक रूपमा संकलन र बिक्रीको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ ।

अघिल्ला वर्षमा करिब ९ लाख टुसा निकासा गरिएकोमा यस वर्ष ६ लाख मात्रै निकासा गरिएको र चोरी निकासी नियन्त्रण गरिएकाले पनि बजारमा टुसाको उपलब्धता कम भएको एक्यापले जनाएको छ ।

उच्च पहाडी क्षेत्रको प्राकृतिक उत्पादन टुसा जडीबुटी मात्र होइन, पोखराको पहिचान बनेको कोसेली पनि हो । तर उत्पादनमा कमी र अवैध निकासी नियन्त्रणको प्रभाव यस वर्ष बजारमा स्पष्ट देखिएको छ ।

संरक्षण र व्यवस्थित व्यवस्थापनसँगै उत्पादन बढाउन सकिए टुसाको व्यापारले स्थानीय अर्थतन्त्रलाई अझ बलियो बनाउने अपेक्षा समेत गरिएको छ ।

articles.title: महारथीको सम्मान लिन नेपाल आउँदै जनरल सेठ
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्धको पुरानो परम्परालाई निरन्तरता दिन भारतीय स्थल सेनाप्रमुख जनरल धीरज सेठ साउन ३१ गते नेपाल भ्रमणमा आउँदैछन् । मानार्थ महारथीको सम्मान पाउने जनरल सेठको यो भ्रमणसँगै गोर्खा भर्ती, अग्निपथ योजना र सीमामा नेपाली नागरिकमाथि हुने व्यवहारका विषय पनि चर्चामा छन् ।

भारतीय स्थल सेनाका प्रमुख जनरल धीरज सेठ पाँच दिने औपचारिक भ्रमणका लागि साउन ३१ गते अर्थात् अगस्ट १६ मा नेपाल आउँदैछन् । नेपाली सेनाका प्रधानसेनापति अशोकराज सिग्देलको निमन्त्रणामा हुन लागेको यो भ्रमणलाई नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्धको निरन्तरताका रूपमा हेरिएको छ ।

भ्रमणका क्रममा जनरल सेठलाई नेपाली सेनाको मानार्थ महारथी दर्जाको दज्र्यानी चिह्न प्रदान गरिने कार्यक्रम छ । सन् १९५० देखि नेपाल र भारतले एकअर्काका सेना प्रमुखलाई मानार्थ महारथीको सम्मान प्रदान गर्दै आएका छन् । यो परम्परालाई दुई देशबीचको विश्वास, मित्रता र सैनिक सहकार्यको एउटा विशिष्ट प्रतिक मानिएको छ ।

यसअघि २०८१ मंसिर २७ गते नेपाली सेनाका प्रधानसेनापति अशोकराज सिग्देललाई भारतको नयाँदिल्लीमा आयोजित विशेष समारोहमा भारतीय राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मुले भारतीय सेनाको मानार्थ महारथीको दज्र्यानी चिह्न प्रदान गरेकी थिइन् ।

नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्ध !

नेपाल र भारतबीचको सैनिक सम्बन्ध शताब्दीयौँ पुरानो मानिन्छ । स्वतन्त्र भारत र नेपालबीच सन् १९५० को शान्ति तथा मैत्री सन्धिपछि दुई देशबीचको रक्षा सहकार्य अझ संस्थागत बनेको हो । दुवै देशका सेनाले संयुक्त सैन्य अभ्यास सूर्य किरण, विपद् व्यवस्थापन, सीमा सुरक्षासम्बन्धी समन्वय, तालिम आदान–प्रदान तथा उच्च तहका भ्रमणलाई निरन्तरता दिँदै आएका छन् ।

यस्तै नेपाली नागरिक भारतीय सेनामा भर्ती हुने व्यवस्था पनि दुई देशबीचको विशेष सम्बन्धको अर्को आधार हो ।

गोर्खा सैनिकका रूपमा नेपाली युवाले करिब दुई सय वर्षदेखि भारतीय सेनामा सेवा गर्दै आएका छन् । अहिले पनि हजारौँ नेपाली नागरिक भारतीय सेनाका विभिन्न गोर्खा रेजिमेन्टमा कार्यरत छन् भने ठूलो संख्यामा पूर्वगोर्खा सैनिकले पेन्सन र अन्य सुविधा प्राप्त गरिरहेका छन् ।

अग्निपथले रोकिएको भर्ति !

तर पछिल्ला वर्षमा भारतीय सेनाको अग्निपथ योजना लागू भएपछि नेपाली नागरिकको भर्ती प्रक्रिया प्रभावित भएको छ । नेपाल सरकारले अग्निपथ योजनाबारे औपचारिक धारणा नटुंग्याएको भन्दै नेपाली युवाको भारतीय सेनामा नयाँ भर्ती रोकिएको अवस्था छ ।

चार वर्षे कार्यकाल र त्यसपछि २५ प्रतिशतलाई मात्रै नियमित सेवामा राखिने अग्गिपथ अन्तर्गतको मापदण्डका कारण लामो समयदेखि कायम रहेको गोर्खा भर्ती रोकिएको हो । यो विषयमा दुवै देशबीच कूटनीतिक तहमा छलफल हुँदै आएको छ ।

सीमा दुखेको सम्बन्ध !

नेपाली सेना र भारतीय सेनाबीच मानार्थ महारथीको विशिष्ट परम्परा रहँदा रहँदै पनि सीमामा भारतीय सीमा सुरक्षा बल एसएसबीले नेपाली नागरिकमाथि गर्ने दुव्र्यवहारका घटना बेलाबेला सार्वजनिक हुँदै आएका छन् ।

एसएसबीले सीमा क्षेत्रमा कुटपिट, अनावश्यक नियन्त्रण, गोली चलाइएका घटना तथा नेपाली नागरिकमाथि भएको दुव्र्यवहारले नेपाली नागरिकले अक्सर भारतसँग चित्त दुखाउनु परेको छ । यस्ता घटनापछि नेपाली पक्षबाट कूटनीतिक विरोध भएपनि दीर्घकालीन समाधान भने हुन सकेको छैन ।

articles.title: वित्तीय क्षेत्रको निष्पक्षता नै अर्थतन्त्रको मेरुदण्डः एक्यान अध्यक्ष नेपाल
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल चार्टर्ड एकाउण्टेण्ट्स संघ (एक्यान) का अध्यक्ष अनुप नेपालले वित्तीय क्षेत्रको निष्पक्षता नै अर्थतन्त्रको मेरुदण्ड भएको बताएका छन् ।

नेपाल अडिटर्स एसोसिएसन (अडान) को वार्षिक साधारण सभालाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा पारदर्शिता र वित्तीय सुशासन कायम गर्न लेखापरीक्षण क्षेत्रको भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण हुने बताए । उनले राज्यको राजस्व सङ्कलनलाई पारदर्शी बनाउन र व्यावसायिक क्षेत्रमा विश्वास अभिवृद्धि गर्न लेखापरीक्षकहरूले गरेको योगदानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

एक्यान र अडान दुवै संस्थाको साझा लक्ष्य नेपाली लेखा व्यवसायलाई थप मर्यादित, पारदर्शी र उत्तरदायी बनाउनु रहेको भन्दै उनले पेसागत हकहित र नीतिगत सुधारका लागि सहकार्य आवश्यक रहेको बताए ।

उनले आजको समय प्रविधिमैत्री युग रहेको भन्दै यसमा पनि अडिटर्सहरुले आफूलाई प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय लेखापरीक्षण मापदण्ड र कर प्रणालीका नयाँ चुनौतीहरूको सामना गर्नका दक्षता अभिवृद्धि गर्नुपर्ने उनको सुझाव छ । पछिल्लो समयको एआई प्रविधिहरुबाट कोही पनि आतंकित हुनु नपर्ने भन्दै प्रविधिलाई केवल एउटा साधनका रूपमा लिन उनले आग्रह गरे ।

उनले क्याल्कुलेटरको आविष्कारको उदाहरण दिँदै क्याकुलेटर आज सामान्य र आवश्यक भएजस्तै एआई जस्ता प्रविधिहरु आगामी दशकमा उस्तै अत्यावश्यक बन्ने बताए ।

खासगरी उच्च व्यावसायिक नैतिकता, निष्पक्षता र इमानदारितालाई आत्मसाथ गरि समाज र राज्यको लेखापरीक्षण पेशाप्रतिको विश्वासलाई मजबुत बनाउनुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिएका छन् ।

articles.title: Health facilities short of essential vaccines, medicines for months
articles.summary:
Patients across Nepal are being deprived of essential vaccines, medicines and health supplements as prolonged procurement and supply problems leave government health facilities with depleted or empty stocks.

The shortages range from iron and folic acid supplements for pregnant women, new mothers and adolescent girls to anti-snake venom, which can mean the difference between life and death for people bitten by venomous snakes. Health facilities have also long reported shortages of anti-rabies vaccines, while the government has yet to vaccinate all vulnerable populations against Japanese encephalitis. This is particularly concerning as the peak monsoon season is ongoing, when the risk of JE and other mosquito-borne diseases increases. Even as the shortage of anti-rabies vaccines has eased, shortages of other essential vaccines are likely to persist for longer.

Health facilities across Bagmati province, for instance, have been without iron and folic acid supplements for months, and this shortage has left thousands of pregnant women, new mothers and adolescent girls without access to the government’s free supply.

Last week, officials from Bhaktapur Hospital and Trishuli Hospital in Nuwakot called the Provincial Health Logistics Management Centre in Hetauda seeking supplies. Other state-run facilities, including primary health centres and health posts, have been contacting the centre for supplies.

But the provincial centre itself has been out of stock for months.

“The responsibility for supplying iron and folic acid lies with the federal government,” Basanta Adhikari, director of the centre, told the Post over the phone from Hetauda. “But federal agencies have not yet supplied us with the supplements. So almost all health facilities in our province are without iron and folic acid.”

Iron and folic acid are among several essential health commodities whose supply has been disrupted by delays in government procurement.

While the shortage of these supplements is unlikely to cause immediate deaths and the tablets are relatively inexpensive and available from private pharmacies, the same cannot be said of some of the other commodities in short supply.

“We have not had a single dose of anti-snake venom for over a month,” said Ujjwal Yadav, information officer at the Provincial Health Logistics Management Centre in Madhesh. “Hospitals and snakebite treatment centres in our province keep calling us for anti-snake venom, but we have no stock. Chief district officers in Dhanusha and Siraha had also contacted us for supplies, but all we could do was tell them sorry.”

The shortage comes during the peak snakebite season. Hospitals and snakebite treatment centres in Koshi, Lumbini, Bagmati, Karnali and other provinces have either run out of anti-snake venom or have only a few vials remaining.

At least 60 people have died and more than 837 have been hospitalised after venomous snakebites since May 14.

The country also faced a shortage of anti-rabies vaccines until last week, raising concerns about access to timely post-exposure treatment. Doctors say rabies can be prevented when vaccination is administered promptly, but the disease is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms appear.

The government is also struggling to provide JE vaccination to all vulnerable populations, even as the mosquito-borne disease continues to claim lives.

Last year, 41 people died of JE. This year, nine people have already died and 37 others have been infected.

The World Health Organisation says the virus kills about one-third of people who develop severe illness, while up to half of survivors are left with severe lifelong disabilities.

Health officials say inadequate funding has prevented the government from administering the JE vaccine to all vulnerable populations at once.

Public health experts say the recurring shortages point to a deeper failure in Nepal’s health system rather than isolated procurement problems.

“The Ministry of Health and Population, now the Ministry of Health and Food Safety, was established to protect people from preventable diseases,” said public health expert Dr Baburam Marasini. “But the incumbent administration appears more focused on concealing the problems and creating the impression that everything is all right.”

“How can things improve overnight when our system remains the same, the budget remains unchanged, and the problems continue to mount?” he said. “The incumbent leadership of the Health Ministry seems to be concealing the problems, and that will prove costly for the country and its people.”

Experts warn that Nepal risks losing hard-won gains in public health built through years of investment if authorities continue to downplay shortages and fail to address weaknesses in procurement and distribution.

The consequences may not always be immediate, they say, but prolonged interruptions in access to essential health commodities can have lasting effects.

The shortage of iron and folic acid, for example, could undermine efforts to tackle Nepal’s persistent burden of anaemia. The free supplementation programme was introduced to reduce anaemia among adolescent girls, pregnant women and new mothers.

According to the Nepal Demographic and Health Survey 2022, around 34 percent of women aged 15 to 49 were anaemic. The prevalence was significantly higher in the Tarai, at 45 percent, compared with 20 percent in the hills and 23 percent in the mountains. Madhesh recorded the highest rate, with 52 percent of women affected.

Anaemia during pregnancy increases the risk of foetal growth restriction, low birth weight, premature delivery and perinatal death. It can also reduce resistance to infection among mothers and babies and impair children's cognitive development.

The government began its iron and folic acid supplementation programme in 2003, after anaemia affected about three in four pregnant women in Nepal in the 1990s.

Under the programme, pregnant women from their fourth month of pregnancy and new mothers up to seven weeks after delivery receive a daily supplement, while girls aged 10 to 19 are provided 26 tablets a year.

Health ministry officials say they have instructed provincial and local governments to purchase iron and folic acid themselves after the federal government failed to procure the supplements on time. But public health experts say shifting the responsibility to lower levels of government cannot substitute for a functioning national supply system.

articles.title: Online attacks targeting minister’s wife highlight deep-seated misogyny
articles.summary:
On the night of August 5, at 9:16 pm, an online content platform named ‘Interviews Nepal’ posted an image on Facebook featuring Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel alongside his wife Susmita Adhikari. The post was shared during an acute cooking gas shortage across the country. It carried a fictional dialogue intended to mock the government’s failure: ‘Sasmit: What does a gas tree look like?’

The uploaded image quickly spread across social media channels as a satirical meme. However, the image was not recent. It was a screenshot extracted from a video recorded during Pokharel’s election campaign some five months ago. Similar repurposed visual materials are frequently used across Nepali digital spaces to criticise the government or the ministers.

When violent clashes occurred between two groups in Sunsari recently, another post featuring the same image appeared on ‘The Nepali Fever’ page. It read: ‘Sasmit! What is happening in Madhesh? Is there a Nepal outside Kathmandu as well?’ By the time of writing, the post had gathered 899 reactions, including 755 ‘haha’ responses. On July 30, at 6:03 pm, a page titled ‘Troll Nuwakot’ published a similar image.

During the Tribhuvan University MBS question paper leak incident, the same image was used with the text: ‘Sasmit! What does a paper leak actually mean?’ A Facebook page named ‘Psycho Nepal’, which commands over 421,000 followers, shared a post stating: ‘Our school madam used to set question papers sitting right in front of us, but they never leaked, Sasmit.’ The comment section beneath the post was filled with similar memes using Adhikari’s picture.

At first glance, such a post may appear to be merely mocking Minister Pokharel. But, more subtly, such trolling is rooted in the same patriarchal mindset that seeks to belittle women, portray them as weak and ridicule them. This is not the first instance of women being subjected to digital trolling or attempts to undermine them online. According to UN Women, women around the world face various forms of online abuse, including cyberbullying, hate speech, trolling, online threats, revenge porn, sexually explicit content created through AI-generated deepfakes and character assassination. The issue is also highlighted in the UN Women's FAQs report published on November 13.

Across these digital platforms, including Facebook, TikTok, Reddit, and Instagram, the memes portray Adhikari as intellectually incompetent. Variations include captions like: ‘Sasmit, how far is Sudurpashchim? Is it west of Thankot?’, ‘Sasmit, the ATM machine drops money so easily, why do people go to work all day?’, ‘Sasmit, do cows produce milk or does the dairy?’, and ‘Sasmit, can’t we collect gold from the Sunkoshi river and distribute it to the poor?’

Though the primary target of public dissatisfaction remains the performance of the government, online users persistently choose Adhikari’s image to express their frustration.

During the parliamentary election campaign, Pokharel drove a vehicle while Adhikari asked him questions regarding law, politics, society, and current affairs, to which Pokharel responded. Following the election, those video frames were isolated and paired with absurd questions designed to undermine Adhikari’s perceived intelligence.

On August 4, at 10:06 pm, a page titled ‘Sad Sarkar Pro Max’ posted an edited image where Pokharel’s face was replaced with former prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal’s. In the edit, Adhikari asks, ‘Sasmit! When will the discussion about our picture end?’ Dahal’s character responds, ‘After death.’

Rights activists argue that these social media trends should not be dismissed as harmless humour. Sabitri Gautam, a prominent women’s rights activist, stated that while the content appears to be political critique, its underlying intention is to target female intellectual capability.

“Citizens have every right to question and criticise the government, and Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel must be held accountable,” said Gautam. “However, targeting his wife instead of him frames women as creatures lacking basic intelligence.”

Kabita Bahing, an advocate and women’s rights activist, said that while meme culture is a modern form of expression, it frequently lacks gender sensitivity.

“Memes are increasingly used to spread hate based on class, gender, caste, physical appearance, skin colour, and sexual orientation,” said Bahing. “This stems from internalised toxic masculinity. Women remain an easy target, and social conflicts are routinely reduced to gendered or caste-based attacks.” She added that society must look beyond the memes themselves and examine the patriarchal mindset driving such digital toxicity.

Political analyst and researcher Sucheta Pyakuryal described such online trolling as a clear reflection of structural patriarchy. “Nepali society remains deeply patriarchal and misogynistic, consistently directing attacks toward women,” said Pyakuryal. “Trolling Susmita instead of focusing on Sasmit is a direct product of this mindset. However, those involved in creating and presenting such campaign materials should have evaluated how these portrayals would impact women’s public image beforehand.”

Youth campaigner Monika Niraula expressed similar concerns, stating that the content is inherently sexist. “I did not find these memes funny because Susmita is the one being continuously ridiculed,” said Niraula. “Her intellectual capacity is being openly questioned. I think it’s misogynistic.”

Niraula observed that female partners of public figures have historically faced disproportionate criticism in Nepal. She cited the example of Arzu Rana Deuba, who is frequently blamed for the political decisions of her husband Sher Bahadur Deuba, the former prime minister.

“She may have her own shortcomings, but the narrative that Deuba's failures are entirely down to her simply isn't fair,” said Niraula.

Political history in Nepal contains previous instances where female figures were targeted with unverified claims to damage political reputations. In May 2013, a monthly magazine named Crime Today published a cover story labelling then CPN (Maoist) leader Hisila Yami as the ‘most corrupt woman in South Asia’.

Following the publication, Yami filed a criminal defamation lawsuit under the Defamation Act against the magazine’s Managing Director Ratna Maya Lama, Editor FR Dahal, Publisher LS Lama, and Indreni Offset Press that printed the magazine. On October 16, 2014, Judge Indra Bahadur Karki of the Kathmandu District Court ruled in favour of Yami, concluding that the news story was published with malicious intent to damage her reputation. The court ordered each defendant to pay a fine of Rs1,000 and compensation of Rs1,000.

Despite the judicial ruling confirming the story was false, online misinformation regarding the claim resurfaced years later. On September 7, 2020, Surya Bahadur Thapa, who was serving as the press advisor to then prime minister KP Sharma Oli, shared a social media post claiming that The New York Times had published a special investigative report in 2013 labelling Yami as the most corrupt woman in Asia. A fact-check published by Nepal Fact Check on the same day confirmed that The New York Times had never published any such report.

Reflecting on these recurring events, Niraula emphasised that Nepali public attitudes towards women in politics have seen little progress over the years. “Hisila Yami’s long political contribution was overshadowed by unverified criticism,” said Niraula. “The mindset remains unchanged today.”

Gautam concurred, noting that gender stereotypes remain entrenched across generations. “Even among the younger Gen Z, the perspective towards women remains largely unchanged,” said Gautam. “What seems like political satire on the surface actually reinforces the idea that women lack intellect.”

Pyakuryal highlighted that the current situation was partly caused by modern political branding strategies, which blur the boundary between private and public life. “Earlier politicians maintained a clear distinction between their personal lives and public duties. The current generation blurs this line in pursuit of political branding, making it difficult to separate private roles from public accountability,” said Pyakuryal. She observed that the campaign video recorded by [Minister] Sasmit reflected a clear gender hierarchy.

“In those videos, Sasmit positioned himself as the knowledgeable figure while using Susmita to ask the questions,” said Pyakuryal. “She was portrayed as someone who needed explanation rather than an expert in her own right. Had she been presented as a strong, informed figure taking a decisive stance, social media users might not have targeted her in this manner.”

Pyakuryal argued that the presentation ultimately exposed Susmita to dual vulnerability. “Susmita has become a double victim of patriarchy. On one hand, her image was used in a subordinate role for political branding. On the other hand, society’s patriarchal and misogynistic elements leveraged that secondary role to launch personal attacks against her,” she said.

articles.title: Rajendra Bimal, literary scholar who sought common ground across Nepal’s divides, dies at 80
articles.summary:
Rajendra Bimal believed that literature could do what politics often failed to do: bring people divided by language, geography and identity into the same conversation.

For decades, the writer, scholar and linguist made that belief the organising principle of his intellectual life. From Janakpur, where he was based for much of his career, Bimal wrote across Nepali, Maithili, Hindi and English, while arguing for a sense of belonging that was larger than any single region, community or language.

Bimal died on Tuesday morning in Janakpur. He was 80.

His oxygen level and pulse dropped suddenly late Monday night, according to his family. He was taken to a local hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment.

To his peers, Bimal was more than a prolific writer. He was an interpreter between Nepal’s literary and linguistic worlds, particularly at a time when questions of identity and belonging were becoming increasingly contested. His work sought neither to erase difference nor to privilege one identity over another, but to find the common ground beneath them.

Born on March 26, 1947, at Devi Chowk in Janakpur-10, Bimal began writing when he was barely 12, publishing his first short story in a Hindi daily. His early interest in languages developed into a lifelong intellectual pursuit. He earned master’s degrees in Nepali, Hindi and Maithili and later completed a doctorate in linguistics.

In 1973, he joined Tribhuvan University as a lecturer of Nepali, beginning an academic career that would span decades. Alongside teaching and scholarship, he produced stories, novels, essays, songs and ghazals in four languages. His writing found its way into classrooms as well as literary circles, giving his ideas an audience beyond the world of academia.

For Bimal, the promotion of Maithili did not mean retreating into linguistic or regional particularism. As founding chairman of the Maithili Development Fund, he worked to preserve and advance the language and its literary traditions while maintaining strong links with the wider Nepali literary establishment.

That bridging role was central to his public life. He became a voice for a broader Nepali identity, one that recognised the country’s linguistic and cultural diversity without allowing those differences to become barriers to dialogue.

His contribution to language and literature earned him the Jagadamba Shree Award in 2010, in recognition of his work helping Maithili-speaking students learn Nepali and his contribution to Nepal’s multilingual literary landscape. He received the Madhupark Honour in 2019.

Surendra Labh, chief of Madhesh Province, described his death as an irreparable loss to the country’s intellectual wealth.

Analyst Chandra Kishore remembered him as a foundational figure in cultural dialogue, particularly for his ability to offer a voice of reason and harmony during periods of social and political fragmentation.

Bimal’s life and work were rooted in Janakpur, but his concerns were never confined to it. He spent his career asking how a country as diverse as Nepal could speak to itself without allowing differences of language, ethnicity or geography to become walls.

His final rites were performed with state honours at the Swargadwari crematorium in Janakpur. His funeral procession passed through several parts of the city and drew federal and provincial ministers, Province Chief Labh, lawmakers, local officials and a large gathering of mourners.

Bimal is survived by two sons and a daughter.

articles.title: Rohit Paudel leaves behind an inspiring legacy as ODI captaincy changes hands
articles.summary:
Rohit Kumar Paudel wanted to play for the senior men’s team after Nepal’s maiden participation in the 2014 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup. Twelve years later, he has lived his dream to a great extent—taking Nepal to two T20 World Cups and becoming Nepal’s most successful captain.

It took Nepal a decade to return to the T20 World Cup. Paudel stood not out at 34 off 20, with Aasif Sheikh (64 off 51), to help Nepal defeat the UAE by eight wickets in the semifinal of the 2024 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Asia Qualifier Final and qualify for the main event.

Similarly, Paudel was the third-highest run scorer for Nepal—scoring 134 runs in six games—in the Asia & EAP Qualifier, from which Nepal progressed to their third T20 World Cup in 2026.

Paudel was not just a crucial player in the two qualifiers for the last two editions of the T20 World Cup, but also led Nepal as the captain.

However, in April 2026, the Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) ended Paudel’s role as the captain of the shortest format and gave the reins to one of the world’s best T20I all-rounders, Dipendra Singh Airee.

Four months later, Paudel has now been stripped of his captaincy in the ODI format as well.

Issuing a statement on Monday, CAN revealed that Paudel has been replaced as the national team skipper in one-day internationals by Sandeep Lamichhane. The governing body of Nepali cricket, however, did not reveal the reason behind the change in captaincy—neither during the change in T20 nor in one-day.

Rohit’s journey so far

Paudel was just shy of 16 when he debuted for Nepal in the ODI against the Netherlands at Amstelveen on August 3, 2018.

In November 2022, Paudel was appointed the captain of the national team after CAN had to drop former captain Lamichhane due to a legal case against him. Paudel’s captaincy then guided Nepal to historic milestones.

Paudel’s captaincy had a quality start as Nepal won 11 of their last 12 League-2 matches in the previous cycle (2019-2023) and finished as one of the top three teams to progress directly to the 2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier.

It was under his leadership that Nepal also qualified for their maiden Asia Cup in 2023. There, Nepal played against India and Pakistan in the group stage.

Paudel’s biggest achievements as the captain of the Nepali team were two consecutive T20 World Cups.

Nepal not only qualified for the T20 World Cup consecutively but also left their mark on the international stage by taking the game to the last ball against the likes of South Africa in 2024 and England in 2026.

And it was again Paudel at the helm when Nepal defeated the West Indies 2-1 in a three-match T20I series in Sharjah last year. It was Nepal’s first bilateral series against an ICC Full Member.

Paudel led Nepal as the captain in 59 T20Is and 63 ODIs. Under his captaincy, Nepal won 33 T20Is and 31 ODIs. He is also Nepal’s longest-ever serving captain. He is followed by Paras Khadka (27 T20Is and six ODIs), Sandeep Lamichhane (18 T20Is and 14 ODIs), Gyanendra Malla (12 T20Is and 10 ODIs) and Dipendra Singh Airee (6 T20Is).

Paudel also has the most caps for Nepal in ODIs. He has played 88 one-day matches for Nepal and is also the one with the most runs in the format. He has scored 2,313 runs in the 50-over game, which include two centuries and 12 fifties.

At 16 years and 146 days old, Paudel became the youngest male batsman in history to register a 50 in One-Day International cricket, after hitting 55 runs off 58 balls against the UAE in January 2019.

In T20Is, Paudel is fourth in the list of players with the most matches for the national team. In 84 T20Is, Paudel scored 1,845 runs, putting him behind only Kushal Bhurtel (2,325 runs in 80 matches) and Airee (2,220 runs in 100 matches).

Paudel has also bagged 14 wickets in T20Is and 11 in ODIs.

Praises pour for Rohit

After the announcement of the change in ODI captaincy, the Nepali cricket fraternity sought one thing: a thank-you post by CAN for Paudel’s contribution to Nepali cricket.

And the cricketing body delivered it on Tuesday.

“Thank you, Rohit, for carrying the hopes of a nation and leading Nepal with passion, dedication and unwavering determination,” CAN wrote on its social media on Tuesday morning. “Your commitment to the team, the country, and the game has always been an inspiration. We are confident that you will continue to serve Nepal with the same spirit, pride, and dedication that you have demonstrated throughout your journey.”

After CAN, several other big names stepped up to thank Paudel.

“Proud of your achievements, your leadership, and the legacy you have left behind as a captain,” wrote CAN secretary Paras Khadka, the former captain who took Nepal to the first T20 World Cup. “Nepal will continue to need you to shine, just as you always have been.”

Likewise, Lamichhane also could not keep himself from recognising the contributions of Paudel.

“Thank you Rohit bhai for everything you’ve done for this team and for the way you’ve led us through every moment,” Lamichhane wrote. “Your contribution, commitment, and presence will always be valued. I’m sure there’s plenty more to come from you in serving this team and the country.”

Similarly, Nepal’s T20I captain Airee had a motivating post for his colleague.

“Some journeys are measured in years, but some leave a legacy that lasts forever… As captain, he did not just lead a team. He inspired a nation, united players, and helped create some of the most unforgettable moments in our cricket history,” wrote Airee. “Many of the achievements we proudly celebrate today carry his dedication, sacrifice, and vision.”

The removal of Paudel from the captaincy role has also been attributed to Nepal’s poor performance in the ongoing ICC CWC League-2.

Recently, Nepal lost all four matches during their League-2 tri-series against Namibia and the Netherlands. It was only the second time Nepal suffered a clean sweep in League-2. The previous one was in the UAE when Nepal lost all four matches against the hosts and the USA.

The loss on Dutch soil was Nepal’s eighth consecutive defeat on foreign soil. Nepal have lost 14 of the 20 League-2 games played abroad in the ongoing cycle (2024-2026). Nepal are currently ranked seventh among eight League-2 teams, have lost the chance to directly qualify for the ODI World Cup’s Qualifier and will be fighting to retain ODI status and fight another long battle to the ODI Qualifier.

But the current League-2 performance cannot shadow what Paudel has led the Rhinos to.

Positive changes?

CAN not only announced the change in captaincy on Monday. It also revealed separate squads for Nepal’s participation at the ACC Premier Cup in Malaysia and the NT Top End T20 Series in Australia. The Premier Cup is taking place from August 30 to September 12, and the Top End Series will be played from August 21 to 30.

Former national cricketers argue that CAN made the changes by keeping Nepali cricket’s best interests at the centre.

“For the last five to seven years, there have not been many changes in the squad,” former national player Sharad Vesawkar told Kantipur. “Despite the changes, we believe that CAN did so for positive results. We hope good results will come.”

Citing two separate squads for the two tournaments, Vesawkar added, “It shows that if you consistently perform in the ‘A’ team, you can open the door to the senior team in no time.”

Meanwhile, regarding captaincy changes, former player Raju Basnyat says that it will not be easy to fulfil the expectations.

“After the Premier Cup, Nepal’s senior team will be busy in the Asian Games and then the Nepal Premier League. After that, a big challenge awaits in League-2 in Oman,” said Basnyat, who is also the head coach of Nepal ‘A’. “The tri-series in Oman is crucial as it directly influences Nepal’s fight to preserve ODI status. It seems that is why CAN made such a shuffle to the squad.”

Basnyat also stresses that a captain is a leader, “and you do not make a leader.”

“A captain is a character,” he added. “Sandeep fits in it. It seems the reason why he was selected.”

articles.title: No more shelving of study commission reports
articles.summary:
Over a dozen commissions and committees have been formed in Nepal in the span of three decades, and largely none of their recommendations has been implemented. This tells the story of how successive governments over the decades constituted high-level panels to probe corruption, atrocities committed during different movements, the grabbing of public land and smuggling, among other issues, only to shelve their reports after they are submitted. In several instances, governments have not even received the reports from these panels.

The unresponsive attitude of successive governments has remained largely unchanged since the 1990s. In May 1990, the interim government led by Krishna Prasad Bhattarai formed a commission under the chairmanship of Janardan Mallik to investigate the loss of life and property and human rights abuses during the People’s Movement. Yet governments that came to power on the sacrifices of dozens of people who fought for democracy took little meaningful action.

The same attitude was repeated after the 2006 People’s Movement. The report of the Krishna Jung Rayamajhi Commission, formed to investigate the suppression of the movement, continues to gather dust, with successive governments showing little interest in implementing its recommendations. There are several other instances in which the Nepali Congress, the CPN-UML and the erstwhile CPN (Maoist Centre) have dumped the reports prepared after extensive study.

The incumbent government is also treading the same path. Ten panels have either been constituted under the Balendra Shah administration or have had their reports come to rest on its shoulders for implementation. Yet none of their recommendations has been fully implemented. The implementation of the Gauri Bahadur Karki commission’s report on state atrocities during the Gen Z movement has so far resulted in the arrest of former prime minister and CPN-UML chair KP Sharma Oli and former home minister Ramesh Lekhak. No progress has been made in implementing the National Human Rights Commission’s recommendations concerning human rights violations during the September 8 and 9 protests, to name just a few.

As Mallik aptly observed, governments have long used such panels to diffuse public outrage and ease political pressure, only to let their reports collect cobwebs once the immediate crisis has passed. The pattern has persisted, regardless of the political transformations the country has undergone over the years.

This is a treacherous betrayal of the people waiting for justice and of the wider public that expects meaningful change based on the findings of such commissions. These investigations often take months and consume considerable state resources, only for their findings to be ignored. Hence, ignorance also amounts to a waste of public resources. Failure to act on their recommendations not only disrespects the experts who served on these panels but also undermines the credibility of the investigative process itself.

More importantly, inaction allows wrongdoing to be repeated with little fear of accountability, deepening the culture of impunity. Had those named by the Mallik Commission been held accountable, those in power in 2006 might have thought twice before using indiscriminate force against peaceful protesters. The same lesson applies to the Gen Z movement.

It is not too late for the Shah government to act. Its commitments to ending impunity and delivering justice will ring hollow if it, too, chooses to shelve commission reports rather than act on their findings.

articles.title: Heirs prepare to strike back
articles.summary:
Similarities between the late Tulsi Giri and Prime Minister Balendra Shah are striking. Both became heads of government in their mid-thirties. Their families were wealthy and highly regarded in the neighbourhood of Janakpur. The Giris are from Siraha and the Shahs from Mahottari, but, like most zamindars of the region, both families maintained a base in the spiritual capital of Mithila.

Giri’s rise—from joining the Nepali Congress to becoming foreign minister and then vice-chairman to chairman of the post-coup Shah regimes in the 1960s—was mysterious, but also spectacular. Beyond his rapid ascent to power, Giri was known among his peers for his exquisite tastes: Bespoke attire, neatly trimmed hair, haute cuisine, fine wines, fast cars and the company of beautiful women.

Shah’s rise has been equally baffling but considerably more dramatic. Within months of the Chartreuse Revolt of 2025, he succeeded in monopolising the Rastriya Swatantra Party, projected himself as a candidate for prime minister, secured a massive majority in Parliament, and became one of the youngest heads of government under a democracy anywhere in the world.

Shah’s platter of cheese, almonds and grapes suggested a healthier, but somewhat similar, appreciation of the good things in life. He dresses with elegant informality: All black, with white sneakers for contrast. Hirsute though he is, he wears his facial hair with élan. Even on the campaign trail, he chose a supporter’s Land Rover Defender over other options. His taste in wines isn’t publicly known. The company he keeps, however, appears to be predominantly male.

Both are professionals who chose unconventional paths before entering politics. Giri was a trained physician who had tried his hand as an innovative restaurateur in Patna, while Shah is a civil engineer who gained fame as a rapper in Kathmandu. It is even possible that Giri’s father knew Shah’s grandfather: Zamindars of Janakpur would occasionally encounter one another at the newly built manor of Bada Hakim Ram Shamsher, just outside the Parikrama Sadak near Kadam Chowk.

The comparisons don’t end there. Giri and Shah are known for speaking little in public. The royal nominee had the reputation of being a patient listener, which is clearly not the case with the republican premier. Giri—labelled the ‘Mother of Panchayat’—could throw tantrums at the all-powerful monarch, resigning over relatively minor issues in the conviction that he would be wooed back on his own terms.

Shah has no such illusions, but he too likes to walk out midway through a presidential address, apparently convinced that everyone had better put up with his idiosyncratic behaviour. Recently, he hit the headlines with a puzzling midnight asocial-media post: “It takes time for the right moment to arrive. It may be delayed, but it won’t be wrong. Don’t worry. Reality can sometimes differ from what is seen and heard. Sometimes one has to fight alone. This is not the first time.” It may not be the last time either, considering that his team of disrupters is failing on all fronts.

Turbulence ahead

With the formal sector stagnant and informal businesses in steep decline, banks have few borrowers as they sit upon piles of cash. Investors’ confidence has hit rock bottom, and remittance continues to be the primary source of income for a significant section of the population. Overall, the economy is in a tailspin. Whatever social cohesion existed in Tarai-Madhesh, especially after the brutal suppression of the Madhesh Uprising in 2015, has begun to fragment further with the sudden and inexplicable spread of Hindutva politics.

On the geopolitical front, the government composed primarily of nepobrats—the urban and entitled kids of beneficiaries of previous regimes—appears to have lost the confidence of old friends without acquiring the trust of new ones: The planned organisation and abrupt cancellation of the 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (IATS) being just one example. The seminar has since been moved online to the embarrassment of its co-hosts in Kathmandu.

In the wake of widespread arson in September 2025 that damaged the presidential secretariat, the Parliament building, central secretariat, the Supreme Court, a premier media house and several prominent businesses, the then-aggressive face of the protests and present Home Minister Sudan Gurung had solemnly declared: “You can burn a Singha Durbar; you can build a thousand Singha Durbars.”

Perhaps there was an expectation of substantial external economic assistance after the regime change, just as there had been after the royal-military coup of 1960? But, as experiences from Afghanistan to Iraq and Sri Lanka to Bangladesh have shown, the equations of the Cold War no longer work. Every country has to clear its mess all on its own.

A placid exterior masking deep internal turbulence offers just the kind of opportunity that adroit political operators seek to rehabilitate themselves. Among the top guns of the post-2015 kleptocratic regime that was violently ousted last year, Pushpa Kamal Dahal appears to be the most sanguine. Perhaps he knows that his utility in history is over. Khadga Prasad Sharma Oli isn’t merely hubristic; he is also narcissistic and unlikely to loosen his grip over his party. A witty description of such ‘regressive communism’ in India’s Cow Belt is ‘Ram-Bam’—a politics that takes pride in an invented past rather than working for an imagined future. It suits the CPN (UML) in Nepal even better.

That leaves Sher Bahadur Deuba—the politician of destiny with neither a sense of history nor any particular belief in his ability to change its course. His scheduled return home after over five months of self-exile following the physical and mental injuries he suffered during the Chartreuse Revolt appears to have energised both factions of Nepali Congress—the establishment and the remnants—in equal measure.

Cardboard crowns

The names of claimants to the leadership mantle of the ‘old NC’, delegitimised through a special convention of the party, fail to inspire. Shashank Koirala, 67, comes from the political dynasty of the Koirala family in Biratnagar. Although a reputed ophthalmologist, he has not been able to offer a vision even for his party, let alone the country.

Prakash Man Singh, 70, is the son of legendary leader Ganesh Man Singh. He has been a lacklustre deputy prime minister. Bimalendra Nidhi, 69, is the son of the late Gandhian leader from Janakpur, Mahendra Narayan Nidhi. Also a former deputy prime minister, his newest claim to fame is accompanying a truck carrying ‘sacred rocks’ excavated from the Kaligandaki River to Ayodhya, where they now lie abandoned in a tin shed.

All these worthies possess names, networks and legacies, but not necessarily the political authority or popular appeal of those from whom they inherited them. The high point of the political tradition they inherited came in 1990, when the king was forced to re-establish multiparty democracy; its nadir came in 2015, when they collectively agreed to kowtow to UML supremo Sharma Oli’s brand of ethnonational majoritarianism.

The ‘new NC’ hasn’t been able to show what’s so new, let alone innovative, in its bag. BP Koirala—a secular agnostic, though not an atheist, and a democratic socialist of international stature in the late 20th century—is the ‘God’ of the party’s official president, whose own legitimacy is now before the court. Yet the latter consciously avoids taking a position on the Hindutva menace.

So, what do the ‘new’ challengers—led by ‘new NC’ President Gagan Thapa, seemingly afflicted with the curse of brilliance—have on offer? More of the same: Sanatan secularism, which is shorthand for so-called ‘soft Hindutva’; prosperity politics instead of socialism; ethnonationalism in the name of nationalism; and majoritarianism in the name of democracy.

Indeed, in the country of the one-horned rhino, the more things change, the more they remain the same. For now, Shah has nothing to worry about except his own party president—but that’s another story altogether. Giri would have resigned. Shah will likely stay put, for now.

articles.title: Young citizens have changed politics. Now comes the test of delivery
articles.summary:
On International Youth Day, Nepal needs more than another celebration of young people’s energy. It needs a practical question: Now that young citizens have altered the country’s politics, can we translate that renewal into wider economic opportunity and institutions that make power deliver?

The youth-led civic movement of September 2025 called for an accountable, responsive government. The election that followed turned that demand into a governing mandate. This was a political agency with national consequence. Yet, changing who holds authority is only the beginning; the larger task is improving what authority produces in everyday life.

This year’s International Youth Day theme, ‘Different Contexts, Common Aspirations’, speaks directly to Nepal. Young people broadly seek quality education, good health, dignified livelihoods, just treatment and a meaningful say in their future. Yet gender, caste, disability, geography, income and care responsibilities shape access to skills, finance, networks and voice.

The 2021 census counted 5.75 million Nepalis aged 15 to 24, nearly one in five people. Of these, 24.6 percent were not in employment, education or training, ranging from 36.7 percent in Madhesh to 17.5 percent in Bagmati. Policy for an imaginary ‘average’ young person will miss both. Inclusive delivery requires common pathways, support proportionate to barriers, and results showing who progresses and who remains excluded.

Agency carries responsibility

Young Nepalis have long contributed to democratic movements, community action, enterprise and civic innovation while seeking a greater voice in consequential decisions. The opportunity now is to turn generational change into better government—through genuine participation, accountable decisions and public action focused on results.

Formal authority comes with office; leadership is demonstrated through action. That work must extend beyond protest and elections into policy, implementation, enterprise and institution-building. This is not a choice between youth and experience. Nepal needs both working together.

Agency carries responsibility, but the burden cannot rest on young people alone. Those of us with authority or expertise must listen, open decision-making space and answer for whether institutions translate aspiration into opportunity. Young citizens have changed politics. The next test is what renewed politics delivers.

Economic opportunity is the test

The durability of political renewal will be decided in everyday economic life. Can education lead to work? Can an idea become an enterprise? Can a capable young person see a credible route to dignity and progress at home?

The Department of Foreign Employment issued 792,187 new and renewed labour approvals in fiscal year 2025/26. Migration has raised incomes, financed education and connected Nepal to the world; it is not simply failure. But choice matters. People should be able to go abroad by choice, not because effort and opportunity remain disconnected at home.

The World Bank estimates Nepal will need about 6.5 million jobs over three decades. No training, credit or start-up initiative can meet that scale alone. Nepal needs complete pathways: education to work experience; skills to employers; enterprises to capability, finance and markets; and local potential to wider opportunity.

The policy direction is clearer. The Sixteenth Plan, formulated by the National Planning Commission (NPC), puts productive employment, entrepreneurship and domestic opportunity at the centre of structural transformation. The government's National Commitment recognises the private sector as the main engine of job creation, with the government creating enabling conditions for investment and growth.

Action has begun. The Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies has adopted a Startup Fast Track action plan, while the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment has approved integrated Employment, Skills and Entrepreneurship Centres. The budget also introduces a National Apprenticeship Programme linking youth to employment-intensive industries through training and private-sector placement. The next task is disciplined implementation and measurable results.

The proposed National Enterprise Facility, led by the Industry Ministry with NPC support, follows the same catalytic logic. It reflects the government listening to startups and acting on policy commitments, particularly around startup capital and growth markets. By using public resources and authority to create an enabling environment and partnerships that multiply capability, finance and market access, the NEF demonstrates a Multiplier Nation: public action crowding in private investment, expertise, diaspora knowledge and local initiative.

Inputs and outputs matter—training, finance, centres and platforms must become operational. But they are milestones. We must also track outcomes—how many people move from learning to earning, how many viable enterprises gain finance and markets, and whether opportunity becomes easier to reach across Nepal.

Leading through uncertainty

Uncertainty operates at every level. Locally, climate shocks, migration and changing livelihoods are reshaping communities. Nationally, demographic change, fiscal pressures and evolving federal institutions are altering development choices. Globally, AI is transforming work, conflicts are disrupting energy and trade, and pandemics have exposed fragile labour and care systems. Aid and trade patterns are also shifting as Nepal approaches graduation from least developed country status.

The outcomes citizens seek remain straightforward; achieving them is not. Public challenges often involve competing interests, behaviour change and coordination across institutions. No expert begins with a complete answer. Leadership requires confidence to set direction and humility to learn during implementation.

We must prepare young people not only for today's jobs, but for problems without manuals. Technical, digital and entrepreneurial skills are essential. So are the capabilities to act with purpose, understand different lives, see systems rather than symptoms and collaborate across differences.

These capabilities shape technology's use. AI can multiply knowledge, speed and reach, but cannot choose which public problems matter, reconcile values or earn collective trust. Technology must remain a tool; human progress must remain the purpose.

Building institutions that deliver

Capable individuals cannot sustain transformation inside institutions that resist learning or rely on exceptional personalities. Individual brilliance is not a development strategy.

In 1972, Aaron Wildavsky published Why Planning Fails in Nepal. His enduring insight was that plans alone cannot create the conditions needed for their success. The constructive lesson today is that sound policy must be matched by institutions capable of learning, adapting and delivering.

The related risk is a capability trap—changing what an institution looks like without improving what it can do. Avoiding it means beginning with real public problems, learning through implementation and judging reform by better outcomes, not procedural completion.

This requires disciplined experimentation, early reporting of problems and operating systems that enable delivery—from recruitment and budgets to procurement, data and performance. Every reform should leave stronger people, processes and relationships. Otherwise, capability has been rented, not built.

The government's commitment to delivery-based governance creates room for this shift. Policy and budgets should respond to lessons from implementation, performance systems should track whether citizens see better results, and successful approaches should expand. National direction must remain clear; implementation should improve through evidence.

International Youth Day should mark a transition from celebrating potential to shared responsibility. Young Nepalis have advanced political renewal. Our task is to multiply economic opportunity, prepare a generation to lead through uncertainty and build institutions that make progress endure.

Political agency can open a new chapter. Economic opportunity will determine whether it lasts; adaptive leadership and capable institutions whether progress becomes cumulative. The unfinished task is not simply to assume power, but to make power deliver, and leave the next generation a state better able to serve.

articles.title: Gas shortages require swift government response
articles.summary:
The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) market in Nepal currently faces a paradox where consumers experience shortages despite government officials claiming that imports from India remain steady. This recurring crisis has resurfaced less than two weeks after the Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) restored the sale of full-sized, 14.2 kg cylinders. The statistics maintained by the NOC tell an interesting story. During the initial stages of the West Asian conflict in February-March, the corporation supplied 51,192 tonnes of gas. LPG supply has remained steady, hovering around 40,000 tonnes per month till June-July. This trend indicates that the volume of fuel entering the country is not the primary driver of the current scarcity.

The roots of the present instability lie in reactive management of gas distribution. Following the escalation of conflict in West Asia in February, the government implemented a rationing system, limiting sales to half-filled, 7.1 kg cylinders to preserve national stocks. This measure successfully managed demand for several months, but the transition back to full-cylinder sales created a sudden, overwhelming surge in domestic gas trade. As the NOC director has acknowledged in a report published in this news outlet, the announcement that full cylinders were once again available caused all previously sidelined empty cylinders to return to the market simultaneously, placing an unbearable strain on the existing distribution infrastructure. This surge was exacerbated by a lack of consumer confidence, leading to panic-driven stockpiling by households and commercial entities.

This market volatility is exacerbated by institutional weaknesses surrounding the regulation of cylinder stocks. It is estimated that there are now approximately 17.5 million LPG cylinders in circulation across Nepal, a substantial increase from the 14.4 million units verified by a 2021 exercise. Despite this massive volume of hardware, there is no comprehensive policy governing how many cylinders a single household or a commercial establishment is permitted to possess. Furthermore, no system exists to determine how many new cylinders should be released into the market annually, rendering the system cluttered and unmanageable. This regulatory vacuum enables those with the means to hoard to do so whenever a perceived shortage occurs, while citizens who possess only a single cylinder are left without any recourse.

The government and the NOC must pursue a series of robust, long-term management strategies to address this crisis.
