Discussions are underway to consolidate the industry, reducing the number of bottling plants from 58 to fewer than 30. Additionally, the NOC is attempting to implement more dynamic distribution monitoring by identifying specific high-demand areas and redirecting supplies on a daily basis to prevent localised shortages. These logistical improvements must be paired with clear legal limits on cylinder ownership to prevent hoarding.

While improving the LPG supply chain is necessary for immediate stability, the most sustainable solution lies in a shift towards energy sovereignty. Given that Nepal is exceptionally rich in hydropower generation, it is strategically unwise to remain heavily dependent on imported fossil fuels. In addition, the recent discovery of natural gas in Dailekh offers another cooking fuel alternative. The government must aggressively promote the adoption of induction stoves and other electric cooking technologies as a primary alternative to cooking gas. By incentivising and subsidising the use of hydroelectricity in households, the state can reduce its import bill, protect citizens from the recurring gas paradox, and leverage its natural resources to ensure a more stable and self-reliant future for every Nepali kitchen.

articles.title: Numa Sambahamphe on the shows and channels she keeps coming back to
articles.summary:
Two twins Qwon & Qjin vlog about fashion, lifestyle, decor, travelling, cooking, learning new skills, and everyday life. They are one of my go to comfort shows to watch. Whenever I feel down or tired or am just resting at home, I go watch them all the time.

The Try Guys are a fun group who basically try everything from games, makeup, cooking, challenges, and even things they’ve never done before. They approach everything like complete beginners. I have been watching them since 2020 and still enjoy everything they put out.

Running Man

It’s a Korean variety show and definitely one of my all-time favourites. I love how chaotic, funny, and unpredictable every episode is, with the cast competing in different games and challenges while constantly making fun of each other. It’s one of those shows I can watch anytime.

One of those shows I’d recommend if you’re into sci-fi, adventure, and a little bit of everything. I love how imaginative the stories are, with time travel, different worlds, strange creatures, and completely unexpected adventures.

The Big Bang Theory

When I am looking for a fun geeky sitcom with a mix of comedy, friendship, and everyday chaos, ‘The Big Bang Theory’ is my ultimate choice. I love the dynamic between the characters and how their completely different personalities somehow work so well together.

One Piece is not just an anime to me; it’s a story that reflects so much of reality, especially when it comes to human emotions, relationships, and the injustices of the world. Beneath all the adventure, humour, and fantasy, there are so many real-life themes that make you think and feel deeply.

articles.title: Taylor Swift wedding-dress fever puts bridal brands on high alert
articles.summary:
Taylor Swift’s wedding dress remains under wraps. But wedding chain David’s Bridal ​is already betting brides will want one just like it.

Fans are eagerly awaiting the reveal of the Christian Dior dress Swift wore at her ‌tightly controlled Madison Square Garden celebration on July 3. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong design team at David’s Bridal, which owns roughly 200 stores across the US, has already sketched about two dozen looks based on the pop star’s likely aesthetics, with a focus on Hollywood glamour and drop-waist silhouettes, CEO Kelly Cook told Reuters.

Those preparations will help the brand “move very quickly when we have an idea of where ​the dress has landed,” Cook explained. David’s Bridal has already seen an uptick in searches for Swift-inspired designs on its website, which lists dresses ranging ​from hundreds of dollars to more than $3,000.

Designers say they will be looking out for elements of her outfit that could blossom into bridal fashion trends.

Viola Chan, head of couture and design at David’s Bridal in Hong Kong, said her team studied Swift’s personal life to sketch three groups of designs: ​embellished ball gowns, simple gowns with a touch of detail, and short dresses in case of a mid-ceremony outfit change.

“It could be her makeup, her hair styling, and could ​be the number of gowns that she changed, the color of her gowns, the floral decoration,” Chan said, while showcasing a template adorned with flowers and lace.

Barcelona-based bridal wear designer Pronovias, with distribution in more than 100 countries, said it plans to draw inspiration from the silhouettes, fabrics and “attitude” of Swift’s look, as the brand has done for royal and other high-profile celebrity weddings in ​the past.

New Swift-Inspired Designs

An unusual color or fabric - pink or metallic lace, for example - could ripple through the bridal industry, said Sharon Sever, the creative director at Tel ​Aviv-based luxury wedding dress company Galia Lahav. A unique veil might also inspire new fashion trends.

For now, brands like Galia Lahav and New York-based Jenny Yoo are in a wait-and-see mode, along ‌with their customers.

“The images make all the difference in the design world,” said Liza Pontoni, design director at Jenny Yoo.

The Justin Alexander Group, a US-based bridal fashion house, is in the process of finalising sketches for its spring and summer 2028 collection, which will be available in stores in autumn 2027. If Swift reveals her Dior dress in the coming weeks, the company might incorporate certain elements into the designs, said CEO and creative director Justin Warshaw.

And if boutiques signal a surge in interest for Swift-inspired gowns, the fashion ​house might pull strings to make the ​new collection available to retailers and brides ⁠even sooner than the typical one-year timeline, Warshaw said.

For indie bridal franchise Lovely Bride, new details will be at most referential to Swift’s look, said Lanie List, the founder and CEO.

“We’ll definitely tell our brides things that we have that are similar, if ​something she wears inspires them,” she said.

Legal Risks

For designers and brands, the risk of falling into legal trouble depends on ​what exactly they copy, said Brad D. Rose, co-chair of law firm Pryor Cashman’s Intellectual Property Group, who works with luxury brands.

US copyright law generally does not protect the cut, shape or silhouette of clothing. That means a bridal company can often lawfully create a dress that mimics an aesthetic. But specific decorative elements such as embroidery or beadwork may be protected.

If a bridal brand were to ​falsely suggest an affiliation with Swift or LVMH-owned Dior, trademark and unfair competition concerns could arise, Rose ​added.

Pronovias leans into seasonal trends rather than emulating specific pieces or names, a spokesperson said.

The designer will, for example, avoid using Swift or Dior’s name in marketing, while still drawing inspiration from trends that emerge ​from the collaboration.

articles.title: What Nepali cinema has changed—and what it hasn’t
articles.summary:
Before the lights dimmed, the audience was already split between two worlds. Some had come to revisit a past they once lived through. Others had only heard stories about it.

The Film Development Board’s ‘Old Is Gold’ offers more than a chance to revisit old Nepali films. The exhibition features ten digitised films, including ‘Aama’, ‘Sindoor’, ‘Pariwartan’, ‘Manko Baandh’, ‘Kumari’, ‘Jeevan Rekha’, ‘Badlindo Aakash’, ‘Ke Ghar Ke Dera’, ‘Shantideep and Hijo Aaja Bholi’.

According to Film Development Board chairperson Dinesh DC, the programme was conceived as more than an anniversary event.

“An anniversary should not only mean cutting a cake and exchanging greetings,” he says. “A good way for an institution to mark its anniversary is also by bringing the history it has preserved back before the public.”

The technical development of Nepali cinema is immediately visible. Camera quality, sound, editing and production have improved significantly over the decades.

In ‘Sindoor’ conversations often unfold through long, largely static shots, while transitions between scenes can feel abrupt to viewers accustomed to the quicker cuts and multiple camera angles of contemporary cinema.

The films preserve not only stories but fragments of everyday life: of streets that no longer exist, fashions long abandoned, accents that have softened with time, and homes built around values that have since evolved.

Songs appear frequently, sometimes interrupting the narrative in ways that can feel excessive today, yet they generated some of the strongest audience reactions. Viewers clapped along when familiar songs began. Among them was Sumit, 37, who had brought his children, aged eight and thirteen, to introduce them to older Nepali cinema. The children said the songs were what they enjoyed most.

DC says that was one of the aims of the exhibition.

“I don’t want to call young people into the hall to give them a history lesson,” he says. “I want them to come, watch the films, enjoy them and start asking themselves questions about what Nepal was like at the time.”

Fashion is one obvious marker of change. Women frequently appear in saris and more traditional attire, contrasting with the broader urban and global influences visible in contemporary Nepali films.

Some romantic conventions now appear exaggerated. During ‘Sindoor’, the audience laughed at prolonged exchanges of glances between the romantic leads that were played seriously in the film.

Yet what now feels clichéd was still being established at the time; films like these helped define conventions later Nepali cinema repeatedly returned to.

At the same time, not everything feels distant. One of the more striking continuities is the way women are represented.

In ‘Aama’, for instance, Harka repeatedly abuses his wife, yet she is still expected to remain within the marriage and endure his behaviour. The scene reflects the limited choices available to women within the social world the film depicts.

Filmmaker and film educator Abhimanyu Dixit says the social shift is more complicated. Older films often relied on archetypes like the dutiful wife, sacrificial mother or “bad woman”, though he notes that some characters still had considerable agency. “Sometimes I watch and think, ‘did we actually become more conservative later?’” he says.

Dixit does not entirely agree that contemporary cinema simply reproduces the same stereotypes in more polished forms. “I actually think contemporary Nepali filmmakers are trying,” he says. “Even compared to 2018, when I used to review Nepali cinema for the Post, I can see a change.”

“You can watch a filmmaker’s work over several films, sometimes even within the same series, and see that their female characters have continued to evolve,” he says. Dixit attributes that partly to the current cultural climate and greater scrutiny from audiences. “Maybe social media scares filmmakers now, so they are more conscious. Or maybe we are genuinely learning.”

DC himself describes old cinema as a “visual document” of its period.

“When we watch an old film, we do not only watch a story,” he says. “We see the cities and villages of that time, the houses, clothes, language, family structures and the way society looked at men and women.”

For older viewers, the films also operate differently.

Sixty-seven-year-old Yogesh Parajuli said watching ‘Aama’ reminded him of a period when going to the cinema itself felt different.

“We used to bunk classes whenever there was a show,” he said. “Our mother used to come and chase us out. This made me miss her.”

That contrast between old and new audiences became one of the more interesting parts of the exhibition. Older viewers often recognised songs, actors and scenes immediately. Younger viewers responded to the films with more distance, sometimes laughing at the acting or dialogue, but still remaining engaged.

For the Board, this is also part of a larger archival project.

DC distinguishes between digitisation, restoration and preservation, noting that the three are not the same. The ten films in the exhibition have been digitised and made suitable for screening, while the Board is also preparing to digitise additional historically significant films.

He argues, however, that preserving only a limited number of films is not enough.

“Ten films are something to be proud of, but we cannot be satisfied with ten,” he says. “This is a beginning, not a destination.”The challenge extends beyond digitisation. Old reels, negatives, scripts, photographs and other material remain scattered across private collections, while copyright and ownership can limit how digitised films are publicly distributed.

Screenings including ‘Aama’, ‘Sindoor’ and ‘Pariwartan’ drew strong attendance, with some shows filling the hall.

For viewers, the exhibition offers a direct comparison between different periods of Nepali cinema. The cameras are sharper, editing is faster, fashion and romance have changed, and filmmakers are reconsidering how women are represented. Yet songs still draw audiences in, familiar storytelling conventions persist, and some older social attitudes remain recognisable.

‘Old Is Gold’ is therefore most interesting not simply as an exercise in nostalgia, but as a record of what Nepali cinema has changed, what it has retained and what it is still learning to leave behind.

articles.title: Exhibit review: Painting the rhythm of Kathmandu’s festivals
articles.summary:
Gallery 108 is showcasing ‘UTSAV: In the Rhythm of the Jatra,’ a solo exhibition by visual artist Pradip Kumar Bajracharya, through Sunday, August 23.

Based in the Kathmandu Valley, Bajracharya draws extensively from the region’s festivals, rituals and living traditions. His works explore how these cultural practices shape collective memory, identity and a sense of community, translating the rhythms and visual richness of traditional celebrations onto the canvas.

‘UTSAV’ brings together a series of paintings inspired by the living festival culture of the Kathmandu Valley—including the Machhindranath Jatra, Bhoto Jatra, and Sindure Jatra—as celebrated in Kathmandu, Patan, Bhaktapur, Hadigaun, and other historic settlements.

Rather than documenting these events literally, Bajracharya’s work seeks to capture their essence, including the rhythm of the dhime baja, the movement of crowds, the colours of celebration, and the devotion of worshippers, translated through brushstrokes, line, colour, and composition.

A distinctive feature of ‘UTSAV’ is its formal unity—every painting in the series has been created in the same square format, a deliberate choice intended to build a sense of rhythm, harmony, and connection across the body of work.

“Art has always been a way of connecting with my culture, my memories, and the people around me,” says Bajracharya, who grew up surrounded by the festivals, rituals, and music of the Kathmandu Valley. “As our society evolves, culture continues to change. While change is natural, it is equally important to preserve the traditions and values that define us.”

Inspired by the belief that art and culture represent Nepal’s true treasures and heritage, ‘UTSAV’ is Bajracharya’s tribute to the living heritage that connects one generation with another.

UTSAV: In the Rhythm of the Jatra

When: Until August 23

Where: Gallery 108, Durbar Marg, Kathmandu

Time: 11 am to 7 pm

Entry: Free

articles.title: Two Nepalis killed on Romanian railway track
articles.summary:
Two Nepalis were killed after being hit by a train in Romania’s eastern city of Bacău early Sunday morning. Their identities have not yet been disclosed.

According to a statement from the Bacău Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (ISU), the two were struck by a train at around 3:21 am while walking along the railway line near Chimiei Street.

Emergency responders, including ambulances, rescue teams and medical personnel, reached the site shortly after receiving information about the incident. They found both individuals dead upon arrival, the ISU said.

Romanian police and railway authorities have launched an investigation into the accident.

“An investigation is underway to establish how they ended up on the railway line and the circumstances that led to the accident,” the ISU said in its statement.

articles.title: Australia tightens student visa rules, rejects 64 percent of Nepali applications
articles.summary:
Australia has rejected around 64 percent of offshore student visa applications from Nepal, marking the highest rejection rate recorded for Nepali applicants, according to official data.

The surge in visa refusals comes after the Australian government tightened its screening process for international students amid concerns over migration levels, housing pressures and the integrity of the education system.

Australia categorises countries under an “Evidence Level” risk framework to determine the level of scrutiny applied during visa processing. Education sector insiders say Nepal was recently moved to “Level 3”, the highest-risk category, from “Level 2” following a government review conducted several months ago.

The impact has been most severe in the vocational education and training (VET) sector, which traditionally attracts students seeking shorter and more affordable courses. Nearly 90 percent of Nepali applications for VET courses have been rejected, with only 56 of 549 applicants receiving visas, according to recent statistics.

Around 60,000 Nepali students are currently enrolled in Australian institutions. Of them, about 56,000 are existing students, while roughly 4,000 are new arrivals.

Data from Australia’s Department of Home Affairs shows a sharp decline in new student arrivals from Nepal. Between January and May this year, only 2,700 of 7,500 offshore applicants from Nepal were granted visas. During the same period last year, 7,167 of 8,028 applicants received approvals.

The uncertainty surrounding visa approvals, combined with rising application costs, has discouraged many prospective students. Applicants currently have to pay an application fee of A$2,500 (approximately Rs260,000), which is non-refundable even if the visa is rejected.

Sanjeev Pandey, a Sydney-based lawyer, said Australia had welcomed a large number of international students after the Covid-19 pandemic, but authorities later became concerned about patterns of students changing courses and extending their stay without completing their original programmes.

“The government may have also tightened student visa rules to address growing employment and housing pressures,” Pandey said.

The stricter visa regime has raised concerns among education consultancies and smaller institutions that rely heavily on international enrolments.

Khagendra Satyal, international business development manager at Central Australian College, said the decline in student arrivals had significantly affected the sector.

“Visas are now granted only after assessing what positive contributions an international student can make to Australia in the long run,” Satyal said. “Students applying from Nepal need to understand this shift.”

The immigration crackdown also comes amid growing political pressure in Australia over migration. Analysts say the rise of politicians with hardline positions on immigration, including Pauline Hanson, has contributed to a broader political push for tighter controls.

Lawyer Pandey said the tougher environment has affected not only prospective students but also those already in Australia. Renewing student visas, switching back to student visas after completing post-study work arrangements, and bringing spouses as dependants have all become more difficult, he said.

Obtaining permanent residency has also become significantly more challenging compared with previous years.

Despite the tightening measures, Nepal remains one of the largest sources of international students in Australia. Government data shows Nepali students account for around nine percent of Australia's international student population, making Nepal the third-largest source country.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Ohio
articles.summary:
Athens is a small, scenic college town in southeastern Ohio, shaped largely by Ohio University and its energetic student community. Surrounded by rolling hills, rivers and forests, the town combines historic streets, local businesses and easy access to nature.

The university campus, downtown shops and restaurants are concentrated within a compact area, making daily life manageable without a car. Ohio University students can also use Athens Public Transit free of charge, while nearby trails and forests provide inexpensive options for hiking and outdoor recreation.

Because Athens is a relatively small town, the number of professional internships available locally can be limited. Although Ohio University hosts career fairs and attracts employers from across the country, students may need to look beyond Athens or relocate temporarily for specialised opportunities.

Oxford is a compact, classic college town in southwestern Ohio, built almost entirely around Miami University at its core. Red-brick Georgian buildings, leafy streets and a walkable uptown give it a traditional campus-town character.

The compact layout means campus, uptown restaurants, shops and student housing are all within easy walking distance. The town is also considered quite safe, and Miami University's strong sense of community brings a steady calendar of campus events, traditions and activities that keep student life active without needing to travel elsewhere.

The town's economy is heavily tied to the university, so it can feel quiet or emptied out during breaks and summer months when students are away.

ColumbusColumbus is Ohio's capital and largest city, and it's where The Ohio State University, one of the biggest campuses in the country, is situated. Rather than a self-contained college town, Columbus functions as a full city with sprawling neighborhoods, a job market, and student population that's just one part of a much bigger urban picture.

Pros:Living costs stay reasonable even with everything a major city offers, and students get real exposure to internships and employers across finance, tech, healthcare and government without having to leave town.

Cons:The scale of the city brings more traffic and scattered housing options, so building a close community takes a bit more intention than it would in a smaller town.

Cincinnati is moving to universities like the University of Cincinnati and Xavier University. The city has 300,000 people and many residential areas.

Pros:The city offers people a diverse job market. It is home to many consumer goods, finance and healthcare companies. The cost of living is on the lower end for cities of this size.

Cons:Despite its universities, the city is not generally considered a college town. Younger residents have to actively seek college-town experiences since it is not part of city life. The city is also not walkable.

Toledo is Ohio’s fourth largest city, sitting on the edge of Lake Erie. It is a city of 600,000 people and home to the University of Toledo.

Pros: The University of Toledo sits at the centre of city life. It is the biggest school in town and also the town's biggest employer. Students have a solid pipeline to work experience and internships.

Cons: As a Rust Belt city, its growth has been stagnant over the years. And despite its size, it is considered to be falling behind the other major metros in Ohio.

Based on conversations with local Nepali students in Ohio.

articles.title: Migrant workers can strike under new Qatari labour law
articles.summary:
The Qatari government has introduced a conditional right for migrant workers to stage legal strikes as part of amendments to the country’s labour law.

Under the revised law, workers can go on strike for up to six working days after notifying their employer and the Ministry of Labour in writing, but only if a labour dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation, conciliation or mediation. The provision was introduced through Qatar’s Law No 9 of 2026, which amended the 2004 Labour Law (Law No 14) to strengthen workers’ rights and welfare.

The amended law requires companies with 100 or more employees to establish joint committees made up of management and worker representatives. The committees are intended to improve workplace dialogue, strengthen consultation and help resolve disputes before they escalate.

The reforms also introduce tougher penalties for labour violations. Employers that breach wage protection regulations may face suspension of ministry services, while the Labour Dispute Resolution Committee has been formally authorised to conduct virtual hearings. Recruitment agencies and companies involved in hiring violations may face fines ranging from QAR3,000 to QAR25,000. One Qatari riyal is equivalent to Rs41.66.

Workers exercising their right to strike will not be entitled to wages during the strike period. The law also allows companies to dismiss without notice workers who organise illegal or unjustified strikes without following the required procedures or who disrupt business operations through such actions.

Companies that fail to establish mandatory joint committees may face fines ranging from QAR2,000 to QAR5,000.

Qatar has also strengthened enforcement of its Wage Protection System. The amended law gives the labour ministry greater authority to take action against employers that delay or fail to pay salaries, including suspending services, imposing administrative measures and applying regulatory penalties against repeat offenders.

If a company repeatedly violates wage rules or triggers collective disputes because of unpaid salaries, other companies under the same ownership may also face penalties. The ministry may publish the names of non-compliant companies on its website.

Workers who remain unpaid can request a change of employer or terminate their contracts, with repatriation costs to be covered by the employer.

The Labour Dispute Resolution Committee’s new authority to conduct virtual hearings means workers no longer need to be physically present to pursue labour cases. Employers, workers and verified witnesses can now participate in proceedings online.

Workers must first register disputes with the ministry. Cases are referred to the dispute resolution committee only when efforts to settle them through negotiation fail. Agreements reached through ministry-led mediation will have the status of legally enforceable documents.

The amended law also increases penalties for recruitment-related violations.

Recruitment agencies can be fined between QAR3,000 and QAR25,000 for hiring workers without ministry approval for employment contracts, processing recruitment before mandatory medical examinations or committing other administrative and recruitment-related violations.

Qatari recruitment agencies generally recruit workers in partnership with manpower agencies in Nepal, although some employers also hire directly through Nepali firms.

The new rules also require workers seeking employment in designated technical and professional occupations to obtain certificates confirming that they have completed required training and passed examinations at ministry-approved centres before starting work.

Meanwhile, Qatar has extended the non-compete period, during which an employee can be restricted from joining a competing company after leaving a job, from one year to two years. The change restores a provision that existed before 2020.

If an employee has access to sensitive client information, trade secrets or confidential company data, an employer can prevent them from joining a competitor for up to two years after the termination of employment.

The labour law amendments are aimed at modernising Qatar’s labour market, improving regulatory oversight and creating a more flexible and competitive employment system in line with the Qatar National Vision 2030. Some provisions will require additional decrees and executive regulations before they come into full effect.

“These reforms represent significant shifts that will heavily impact employers, workers, recruitment agencies and the dispute resolution system alike,” Krishna Panthi, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association Qatar, told Kantipur.

articles.title: कोलम्बियामा शक्तिशाली भूकम्प : मृत्यु हुनेको संख्या २५० नाघ्यो, उद्धार कार्य जारी
articles.summary:
पश्चिमी कोलम्बियामा गएको यस शताब्दीकै विनाशकारी ७.४ म्याग्निच्युडको भूकम्पमा परी ज्यान गुमाउनेको संख्या २५० नाघेको छ। सोमबार बिहान गएको यस शक्तिशाली भूकम्पले कफी उत्पादन गर्ने मुख्य क्षेत्रहरूमा ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ।

भग्नावशेषमा अझै पनि मानिसहरू फसेको आशंकामा उद्धार टोलीहरूले क्रेन, उत्खनन मेसिन र आफ्नै नांगो हातले खोज तथा उद्धार कार्य जारी राखेका छन्। भग्नावशेषमुनिबाट जीवितै मानिसको आवाज सुन्न सकियोस् भनेर उद्धारकर्मीहरूले बेलाबेलामा पूर्ण रूपमा शान्त रहन आग्रह गर्दै आएका छन्। प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा मानिसहरूले मानवी साङ्लो बनाएर बालुवा र भग्नावशेषका बाल्टिनहरू हटाउने काम गरिरहेका छन्।

भूकम्पका कारण पेरेरा, काली र चोकोलगायतका क्षेत्रमा सयौँ अपार्टमेन्ट, घर, विद्यालय र अस्पतालहरू भत्किएका छन्। यस विपद्‌मा परी हजारौँ मानिसहरू घरबारविहीन बनेका छन् भने कतिपय क्षेत्रमा अझै पनि सञ्चार र विद्युत् सेवा अवरुद्ध छ।

घटनास्थलमा खटिएका स्थानीय नागरिक जोस ग्यालेगोले भने, ‘मैले पैदलै सहर पार गरें, दुई घण्टा लाग्यो र दृश्यहरू अत्यन्तै विनाशकारी थिए। यो जीवनमा आएको दुःस्वप्न जस्तै थियो।’

यसैबिच, कोलम्बियाका राष्ट्रपति एबेलार्डो डे ला एस्प्रिएलाले प्रभावित क्षेत्रको अवलोकन गर्दै राहत र आर्थिक सहयोगको घोषणा गरेका छन्। स्थानीय प्रशासन र उद्धारकर्मीहरूले पहिलो ४८ देखि ७२ घण्टा उद्धारका लागि अति महत्वपूर्ण हुने बताएका छन्।

articles.title: ‘थर्मल ड्रोन’को सहायताबाट चितुवालाई नियन्त्रणमा लिइँदै
articles.summary:
डिभिजन वन कार्यालयले मानव बस्ती र आसपासका क्षेत्रमा रहेका दुई चितुवा अनुगमन र नियन्त्रणका लागि ‘थर्मल ड्रोन’को सहायता लिएको छ।

कार्यालय र राष्ट्रिय प्रकृति संरक्षण कोषको संयुक्त टोलीलले विगत दुई दिनदेखि कृषि तथा वन विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालयको क्षेत्रमा रहेको झाडीमा चितुवा हुनसक्ने आकलन गर्दै ड्रोनको सहायता लिएको हो। विगत दुई महिनादेखि भरतपुर महानगरपालिका–१५ र कृषि तथा वन विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालयको परिसरमा रहेको झाडीमा चितुवा देखिएपछि नियन्त्रणको काम सुरु गरिएको हो।

दिनको समयमा नदेखिने रातको समयमा देखिने गर्दा नियन्त्रणमा लिन कठिन भएको कार्यालयका सूचना अधिकारी देवीप्रसाद पौडेलले जानकारी दिए। अहिले चितुवा नियन्त्रणका लागि दिउँसोमा थर्मल ड्रोन (वन्यजन्तुको तापक्रम पहिचान गर्न सक्ने), पाँच स्थानमा सिसीक्यामेरा जडान, तीन स्थानमा खोर ट्यापिङ, तीन स्थानमा खुट्टा ट्यापिङ (खुट्टा अल्झाउन) का लागि काम गरिएको उनले जानकारी दिए।

चितुवा नियन्त्रणका लागि डिभिजन वन कार्यालय चितवन र राष्ट्रिय प्रकृति संरक्षण कोषका प्राविधिक टोली खटिएको उनले बताए। ती खोर ट्यापिङको काम चितुवालाई सहज हुनेगरी राखिएको छ। अहिले सो क्षेत्रमा एउटा माउ र एउटा बच्चा चितुवा रहेको उनले जानकारी दिए।

उनका अनुसार एउटा बच्चा चितुवा भरतपुर–१५ बाट नियन्त्रणमा लिइसकिएको छ। सो बच्चालाई राष्ट्रिय प्रकृति संरक्षण कोषमा लगरे राखिएको छ। चितुवाको पाइलाका आधारमा खोरहरू स्थानान्तरण गरेर राख्ने गरिएको छ। सो कार्यमा लागेका डिभिजन वन कार्यालयका वन अधिकृत सुदीप हमालका अनुसार कृषि तथा वन विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय रामपुर परिसरको गाई अनुसन्धान कार्यक्रमको आवास क्षेत्रमा दुईपटक चितुवा देखिएको छ।

सिसीक्यामेरामा एक साताअघि एउटा र आइतबार राति दुईवटा चितुवा देखापरेको उनले जानकारी दिए। सोपश्चात सो क्षेत्रमा थर्मल ड्रोनको प्रयोग गरिएको भए पनि चितुवा भेट्न सकिएको छैन। उनका अनुसार सो ठाउँमा खोर र खुट्टा ट्यापिङ पनि राखिएको छ।

यस्तै वन क्याम्पस नजिक एउटा र भरतपुर महानगरपालिका–१५ को अविनास पोल्ट्री परिसरमा एउटा खोर राखिएको छ। विभिन्न ठाउँमा क्यामेरासमेत राखिएको उनले बताए। चितुवाको आवतजावत भएको क्षेत्रमा क्यामेरा राखिएको छ।

यस्तै भरतपुर–११ स्थित आँपटारीमा रहेको विद्युत् स्टेसन क्षेत्रमा बाघ देखिएको जनाउँदै कर्मचारीले गुनासो गरेपछि दुईवटा क्यामेरा जडान गरिएको छ। बाघले स्थानीयको बाख्रा खाएको जनाइएको छ। सो क्यामेरामार्फत अनुगमन भइरहेको अधिकृत हमालले जानकारी दिए।

articles.title: युवा प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई युवा आकांक्षा चुनौती
articles.summary:
संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले तय गरेको ‘फरक पृष्ठभूमि, साझा आकांक्षा’ भन्ने नारासहित आज बुधबार विश्वभर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवस मनाइँदै छ। यो नाराले विश्वका विभिन्न सामाजिक, आर्थिक र भौगोलिक परिस्थितिमा रहेका युवाका साझा आकांक्षा गुणस्तरीय शिक्षा, मर्यादित रोजगारी, निर्णय प्रक्रियामा सहभागिता र राम्रो भविष्य निर्माणको चाहना र अवसरलाई केन्द्रमा राखेको छ।

नेपालमा गत भदौमा जेनजी (युवा) को सहभागितामा आन्दोलन भयो। त्यसपछि फागुनमा भएको संघीय प्रतिनिधिसभाको निर्वाचनले मुलुकको कार्यकारी प्रमुखको जिम्मेवारी युवा पुस्तामा पुर्‍याएको छ। नेता बन्नु र नेतृत्वमा पुग्नु ठुलो कुरा होइन तर युवाको आकांक्षा, विभिन्न क्षेत्रमा सहभागिता, क्षमता विकास र अवसरको समान वितरणलाई व्यवहारमा उतार्नु वर्तमान सरकार र प्रधानमन्त्रीको मुख्य चुनौती बनेको छ।

३६ वर्षीय बालेन्द्र शाह प्रधानमन्त्री छन्। उनीबाट नयाँ पुस्ताले सुशासन, रोजगारी, भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रण, प्रविधिमैत्री शासन, अवसरको समान वितरणजस्ता विषय कार्यान्वयन तहमा आउने अपेक्षा गरेको छ। युवाले अत्यन्त नजिकबाट सरकारका गतिविधिलाई हेरिरहेका छन्।

युवा शक्ति, अवसर र सम्भावना

नेपाल अहिले जनसांख्यिक लाभको महत्त्वपूर्ण चरणमा छ। संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघका अनुसार नेपालमा १५ देखि २४ वर्ष उमेर समूहको जनसंख्या करिब ५७ लाख छ, जुन कुल जनसंख्याको करिब २० प्रतिशत हो। नेपालको फराकिलो परिभाषाअनुसार १६ देखि ४० वर्ष उमेर समूहलाई युवा मान्दा यो हिस्सा झन्डै ४३ प्रतिशत पुग्छ।

युवा शक्तिलाई उपयोग गर्न नसके नेपाल ‘युवा राष्ट्र बन्न नपाउँदै वृद्ध राष्ट्र बन्ने’ जोखिम छ। जनसांख्यिक लाभांशको समय सीमित हुन्छ। काम गर्ने उमेर समूहको ठुलो हिस्सा हुँदा शिक्षा, सीप, रोजगारी र उत्पादनशील क्षेत्रमा लगानी गर्न नसकेपछि यही जनसंख्या केही दशकपछि वृद्ध जनसंख्यामा परिणत हुन्छ र देशले आर्थिक लाभ लिन सक्दैन।

सरकारले गत वर्ष युवाको भूमिका र आवश्यकता सम्बोधन गर्न राष्ट्रिय युवा नीति ल्याएको छ। नयाँ नीतिले युवालाई विकास प्रक्रियाको सक्रिय साझेदारका रूपमा हेर्दै शिक्षा, सीप, रोजगारी, उद्यमशीलता, नेतृत्व विकास र सामाजिक सहभागितालाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेको छ।

चुनौती: विदेश पलायन

नेपालका लागि सबैभन्दा ठुलो चुनौती युवाको विदेश पलायन हो। रोजगारी र अवसरको खोजीमा युवा विदेश जाने क्रम जारी छ। एकातर्फ यसले तत्कालका लागि विप्रेषणमार्फत अर्थतन्त्रलाई टेवा दिएको छ भने अर्कातर्फ देशभित्र उत्पादनशील जनशक्ति अभाव हुने जोखिम बढाएको छ। सरकारी तथ्यांकअनुसार सन् २०२१ देखि २०२५ सम्म वैदेशिक रोजगारीका लागि हरेक वर्ष सरदरमा साढे सात लाख हाराहारी नेपाली बिदेसिएका छन्।

त्यस्तै अध्ययनका लागि जाने युवाको संख्या हरेक वर्ष एक लाख हाराहारी छ। यस्तो अवस्थामा युवालाई विदेश जान रोक्ने नीतिभन्दा पनि नेपालमै अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने नीति राज्यको हुनुपर्छ। कृषि, सूचना प्रविधि, पर्यटन, हरित अर्थतन्त्र, नवप्रवर्तन र साना तथा मझौला उद्यममा युवाको लगानी र सहभागिता बढाउने वातावरण बनाउनु पर्छ।

राष्ट्रिय योजना आयोगको अगुवाइमा राष्ट्रिय रोजगारी नीति बनाएर वार्षिक एक लाख युवालाई रोजगारी सिर्जना गर्ने तयारी भइरहेको बताउँछन् राष्ट्रिय युवा परिषद्का प्रशासकीय प्रमुख गेहनाथ गौतम। ‘सरकारको यो नीति र कार्यक्रमले युवालाई रोजगारीका अवसर सिर्जनामा योगदान गर्ने छ,’ उनले भने, ‘सरकारले मात्रै रोजगारी सिर्जना गर्न सक्दैन। सरकारले त सहजीकरण गर्ने हो। यसमा निजी क्षेत्रको भूमिका अहं हुन्छ।’

युवा आकांक्षा र अवसरबिच बढ्दै दुरी

युएनएफपिएले गत महिना सार्वजनिक गरेको ‘डेमोग्राफिक फ्युचर सर्भे’मा विश्वका ७३ देश तथा विभिन्न क्षेत्रका इन्टरनेटमा पहुँच भएका १८ देखि ३९ वर्ष उमेर समूहका एक लाख आठ हजार बढी युवाको धारणा समेटेको छ।

विश्वकै ठुला सर्वेक्षणमध्ये एक मानिएको यो सर्भेमा विश्वभरका युवाले अर्थपूर्ण भविष्य, स्थिर सम्बन्ध र धेरैका लागि परिवार निर्माणको आकांक्षा राखेको देखिएको छ तर बढ्दो अनिश्चितताबिच उनीहरूले जीवनका महत्त्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिनुपरिरहेको छ। महँगिँदो आवास, आर्थिक असुरक्षा, द्वन्द्व, असमानता र तीव्र प्राविधिक परिवर्तनले युवाले कसरी भविष्य परिकल्पना गर्ने र योजना बनाउने भन्नेमा प्रभाव पारिरहेको छ।

युएनएफपिएको सर्वेक्षणले एउटा स्पष्ट निष्कर्ष देखाएको छ– धेरै युवा अझै पनि प्रेम सम्बन्ध, विवाह र अभिभावकत्वको आकांक्षा राख्छन्। प्रश्न युवाले यस्ता जीवनका लक्ष्यलाई महत्त्व दिन्छन् कि दिँदैनन् भन्ने होइन, ती आकांक्षा पूरा गर्न आवश्यक सामाजिक र आर्थिक अवस्था उनीहरूसँग छ कि छैन भन्ने हो। आर्थिक सुरक्षा, स्थिर रोजगारी, किफायती आवास र आवश्यक सामाजिक सहयोगले युवाको जीवन निर्णयमा महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निर्वाह गर्ने सर्वेक्षणले देखाएको छ। यसले युवा आकांक्षा र उनीहरूले खोज्ने अवसरबिच ठुलो अन्तर रहेको देखाउँछ।

सर्वेक्षणले जनसांख्यिक प्रवृत्तिलाई मात्र हेर्नुभन्दा युवाका छनोटलाई प्रभावित गर्ने आधारभूत अवस्थातर्फ ध्यान दिनुपर्ने पनि औंल्याएको छ। रोजगारीका अवसर र सुरक्षा, किफायती आवास, सहज बाल हेरचाह, लैंगिक समानतामा आधारित अभिभावकीय बिदा, लचिलो कामको व्यवस्था र समग्र लैंगिक समानता युवालाई आफूले चाहेको जीवन निर्माण गर्न सक्षम बनाउने महत्त्वपूर्ण आधार हुन्।

नेपालका लागि युएनएफपिए सर्वेक्षणको निष्कर्ष अझ बढी सान्दर्भिक छ। कामको अभाव र आर्थिक असुरक्षाका कारण ठुलो संख्यामा नेपालका युवा बिदेसिने गरेका छन्। यो सन्दर्भमा ती युवाले आफूले चाहेको शिक्षा, रोजगारी, परिवार र भविष्य निर्माण गर्ने अवसर पाएका छन् कि छैनन् भन्ने प्रश्न महत्त्वपूर्ण छ। युवा जनसंख्यालाई उत्पादनशील शक्तिमा रूपान्तरण गर्न नसके लाभ लिन कठिन हुन्छ।

अबको बाटो के?

सम्बद्ध विज्ञका अनुसार नेपालले रोजगारी सिर्जना, सीप र शिक्षामा सुधार, हरेक क्षेत्रमा युवाको अर्थपूर्ण सहभागिता, नवप्रवर्तन, उद्यमशीलता र विदेशमा रहेका युवाको ज्ञान र पुँजी उपयोगमा ध्यान दिन जरुरी छ। हरेक वर्ष श्रमबजारमा प्रवेश गर्ने युवालाई लक्षित गर्दै उत्पादनशील क्षेत्रमा लगानी बढाउन आवश्यक छ, जुन सरकारी र निजी क्षेत्रबिचको सहकार्यबाट मात्र सम्भव छ। परम्परागत शिक्षाले मात्र बदलिँदो विश्व बजारको आवश्यकता पूरा गर्न नसक्ने र यसका लागि सीप र शिक्षामा सुधार हुनुपर्ने विज्ञ मत छ।

नयाँ सरकारप्रति युवाको ज्यादै धेरै अपेक्षा छ। तर सरकारले चार महिनामा अपेक्षित काम गर्न नसकेको भन्दै प्रश्न उठाउन थालिएको छ। यसलाई स्वीकार गर्दै युवा श्रम तथा रोजगारमन्त्री रामजी यादवका प्रमुख सल्लाहकार शंकर श्रेष्ठ शुसासन कायम गरेर आर्थिक तथा रोजगारीका आधार सिर्जना गर्नेतर्फ सरकार लागिपरेको बताउँछन्। ‘राष्ट्रिय रोजगारी नीतिको तर्जुमासँगै राष्ट्रिय युवा परिषद् ऐन पनि परिमार्जन हुँदैछ। गत वर्ष ल्याइएको राष्ट्रिय युवा नीति कार्यान्वयनमा यसले सहयोग गर्नेछ,’ उनी भन्छन्।

उनले युवा स्वरोजगार कार्यक्रमलाई पनि यही ऐनअन्तर्गत ल्याउने तयारी रहेको बताए। ‘हामीसँग वैदेशिक रोजगारी प्रवर्धन बोर्ड छ तर स्वदेशमा रोजगारी सिर्जना गर्न पनि यस्तैखाले बोर्ड चाहिन्छ। समग्रमा रोजगारी प्रवर्धनमा सरकार लागेको छ,’ उनी भन्छन्।

सरकारले प्राप्त अवसरलाई उपयोग गर्न सके युवा जनसंख्यालाई विकास शक्तिमा बदल्न सक्छ। अन्यथा यही युवा शक्ति निराशा र पलायनको स्रोत बन्न सक्छ।

articles.title: संसद्‌मा किन पुग्दैन गणपूरक संख्या ? मन्त्रालय धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यता रहेको सांसद तामाङको स्पष्टोक्ति
articles.summary:
प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठकमा आवश्यक गणपूरक संख्या नपुगेर महत्वपूर्ण विधेयक अघि बढ्न नसकेपछि सांसदहरूको उपस्थिति र सदनमा हुने बहसमाथि प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ।

यसैबिच राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) की सांसद आशिका तामाङले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत सांसदहरू केवल हाजिरी जनाएर सदनबाट बाहिरिने बाध्यता रहेको बताएकी छिन्। उनले लेखेकी छन्, ‘हाजिर गर्‍यो अनि टाप रे ? सदन भनेको ७ घण्टासम्म ठिक हो।’ उनका अनुसार सदनमा लामो समयसम्म बहस हुनु आफैमा गलत होइन तर त्यस्तो बहस ठोस, तथ्यपरक र कार्यान्वयनमुखी हुनुपर्छ।

उनले थप लेखेकी छन्, ‘जे बोल्नुपर्ने ठोस र तथ्यपरक कुरा उठाउने र कार्यान्वयन गर्न निर्देशिका दिने खालको भए पो त।’ तामाङले प्रतिपक्षका सांसदहरूले बोल्ने क्रममा एउटै विषय पटकपटक दोहोर्‍याउने प्रवृत्तिप्रति पनि असन्तुष्टि जनाएकी छन्। सभामुखले समय सकिएको जानकारी गराउँदा पनि समय थप माग्ने र नयाँ विषय नउठाई एउटै कुरा दोहोर्‍याइरहने अवस्था भए सदनको बहस लामो र नीरस बन्ने उनको तर्क छ। उनले प्रश्न गरेकी छन्, ‘नयाँ कुरा केही छैन, एउटा कुरा दोहोर्‍याको दोहोर्‍यै ! अनि लामो हुँदैन र, नीरस हुँदैन त?’

हिजो प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठकमा आवश्यक गणपूरक संख्या नपुगेपछि विधेयक पेस हुन नसकेको घटनाले सांसदहरूको नियमित उपस्थितिको विषयलाई चर्चामा ल्याएको छ। सांसदहरू सदनमा उपस्थित भएर आफ्ना धारणा राख्नु लोकतान्त्रिक अभ्यासको महत्वपूर्ण पक्ष भए पनि हाजिरी जनाएर बैठकमा सहभागी नहुने प्रवृत्तिले संसदको कामकारबाहीमा असर पार्न सक्ने देखिएको छ।

सांसद तामाङले सांसदहरू मन्त्रालयहरू धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यताका कारण पनि संसदमा संख्या नपुग्ने गरेको प्रष्ट पारेकी छिन्। उनले भनिन्, ‘अब सांसदहरू सबै मन्त्रालयको ढोकामा कतिखेर मन्त्री र सचिवलाई भेट्ने अनि गुनासो पोख्ने भनेर लाइनमा हुनुहुन्छ अनि पुग्छ त संख्या ?’ सरकार फेरिए पनि र प्रधानमन्त्री नयाँ आए पनि काम गर्ने कर्मचारीले नै हो भन्दै उनले जनताका गुनासा लिएर सम्बन्धित मन्त्रालय र मन्त्रीलाई भेट्न समयमै भौतारिनुपर्ने बाध्यता रहेको बताइन्।

त्यसैले सदनमा सांसदको उपस्थितिसँगै बहसको गुणस्तर पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुने देखिन्छ। लामो समयसम्म बोल्नुको सट्टा जनताका वास्तविक समस्या, तथ्य र समाधानका उपायसहितको बहस गर्ने तथा त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयनमा लैजाने वातावरण बनाउनुपर्ने आवश्यकता औंल्याइएको छ।

articles.title: कोलम्बियामा शक्तिशाली भूकम्प : मृत्यु हुनेको संख्या २५० नाघ्यो, उद्धार कार्य जारी
articles.summary:
पश्चिमी कोलम्बियामा गएको यस शताब्दीकै विनाशकारी ७.४ म्याग्निच्युडको भूकम्पमा परी ज्यान गुमाउनेको संख्या २५० नाघेको छ। सोमबार बिहान गएको यस शक्तिशाली भूकम्पले कफी उत्पादन गर्ने मुख्य क्षेत्रहरूमा ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ।

भग्नावशेषमा अझै पनि मानिसहरू फसेको आशंकामा उद्धार टोलीहरूले क्रेन, उत्खनन मेसिन र आफ्नै नांगो हातले खोज तथा उद्धार कार्य जारी राखेका छन्। भग्नावशेषमुनिबाट जीवितै मानिसको आवाज सुन्न सकियोस् भनेर उद्धारकर्मीहरूले बेलाबेलामा पूर्ण रूपमा शान्त रहन आग्रह गर्दै आएका छन्। प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा मानिसहरूले मानवी साङ्लो बनाएर बालुवा र भग्नावशेषका बाल्टिनहरू हटाउने काम गरिरहेका छन्।

भूकम्पका कारण पेरेरा, काली र चोकोलगायतका क्षेत्रमा सयौँ अपार्टमेन्ट, घर, विद्यालय र अस्पतालहरू भत्किएका छन्। यस विपद्‌मा परी हजारौँ मानिसहरू घरबारविहीन बनेका छन् भने कतिपय क्षेत्रमा अझै पनि सञ्चार र विद्युत् सेवा अवरुद्ध छ।

घटनास्थलमा खटिएका स्थानीय नागरिक जोस ग्यालेगोले भने, ‘मैले पैदलै सहर पार गरें, दुई घण्टा लाग्यो र दृश्यहरू अत्यन्तै विनाशकारी थिए। यो जीवनमा आएको दुःस्वप्न जस्तै थियो।’

यसैबिच, कोलम्बियाका राष्ट्रपति एबेलार्डो डे ला एस्प्रिएलाले प्रभावित क्षेत्रको अवलोकन गर्दै राहत र आर्थिक सहयोगको घोषणा गरेका छन्। स्थानीय प्रशासन र उद्धारकर्मीहरूले पहिलो ४८ देखि ७२ घण्टा उद्धारका लागि अति महत्वपूर्ण हुने बताएका छन्।

प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा क्षतिको पूर्ण विवरण संकलन गर्ने र राहत वितरण गर्ने काम पनि जारी छ। एजेन्सी

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: Nepal Police seeks call interception powers, reviving privacy and civil liberties concerns
articles.summary:
Nepal Police has asked the government to give it legal authority to intercept telephone calls and digital communications in real time during criminal investigations, reopening a long-running debate over how far the state should be allowed to ‘intrude’ into citizens’ private communication.

The Police Headquarters in Naxal has incorporated the proposal into its strategic planning framework, arguing that investigators need modern digital tools to pursue criminals who increasingly use encrypted and other sophisticated communication technologies.

The proposal would allow designated police officers to listen to telephone conversations and monitor digital communications in real time if the necessary legal framework and approvals were put in place.

“Individuals involved in heinous crimes or those evading justice often employ advanced technologies, making it necessary for us to listen in on communications when probing serious offences,” Deputy Inspector General Abi Narayan Kafle, central spokesperson for Nepal Police, told Kantipur. “We have prepared a comprehensive plan to make police investigations technology-friendly and have already briefed the Ministry of Home Affairs on this operational strategy.”

Police officials say the proposed power would be aimed at serious criminal investigations rather than broad surveillance. But the request has revived concerns among lawyers and civil rights activists over the possibility of political or institutional abuse, particularly given Nepal’s history of political interference in security and law enforcement agencies.

The proposal also echoes previous attempts by state agencies to obtain wider surveillance powers, which were abandoned after strong opposition from lawmakers, rights activists and civil society groups.

The National Investigation Department, the country’s principal civilian intelligence agency, had previously sought similar authority through proposed legislation. Draft legislation concerning the department had included provisions allowing authorities to monitor, track and intercept phone calls, text messages and video communications.

Section 15 of the proposed intelligence bill would have allowed the chief research officer to order the interception of electronic communications when other intelligence-gathering methods were considered impractical and when failure to intercept the communications was deemed to pose an immediate threat to national security.

The proposal drew widespread criticism over the potential for abuse. Political opposition and public concern eventually forced the government to abandon the bill.

The latest push by the police comes against a different backdrop. Law enforcement officials argue that criminals have become increasingly adept at using technology to conceal their activities, making access to communications an important investigative tool.

But legal experts say any such authority would have to be tightly circumscribed by law and subjected to independent judicial oversight.

Senior Advocate Satish Krishna Kharel, an expert in criminal law, said the potential risks of live interception are considerably greater than those associated with obtaining call detail records or SMS logs.

Police already need judicial authorisation to obtain such records, he said. Allowing investigators to listen to conversations as they happen would create a much greater intrusion into an individual’s privacy.

“Without stringent statutory criteria and robust judicial oversight, this kind of power is exceptionally susceptible to abuse,” Kharel told Kantipur. “Given that agencies like Nepal Police and the NID have historically faced intense political pressure, granting the power to live-tap any citizen’s phone directly compromises the right to privacy guaranteed under Article 28 of the constitution.”

Article 28 of the constitution guarantees the privacy of an individual’s body, residence, property, documents, data, correspondence and personal character. Any law allowing the state to intercept communications would therefore have to operate within those constitutional protections.

The question of how police obtain telecommunications data has already been tested by the Supreme Court.

Before the court intervened, police had obtained call detail records and SMS data through informal arrangements with telecommunications companies, both private and state-owned. That practice came under intense scrutiny after the assassination of Supreme Court Justice Rana Bahadur Bam on May 31, 2012.

During the investigation into the killing, police collected more than 500,000 call records and over 30,000 text messages in an effort to identify the perpetrators.

The broad collection of communications data failed to identify the actual killer while exposing the personal information of thousands of people who had no connection to the crime.

In a landmark ruling, a joint bench of then-Chief Justice Kalyan Shrestha and Justice Devendra Gopal Shrestha held that the need to investigate a crime did not give the state unrestricted authority to access citizens’ communications data.

The ruling established judicial authorisation as a necessary safeguard for obtaining such information, reinforcing the principle that investigative necessity cannot override the constitutional right to privacy.

The judgment has since become an important reference point in discussions about state access to telecommunications data.

Former Inspector General of Police Dhiraj Pratap Singh acknowledged that police had faced disciplinary scrutiny in the past over the improper use of call detail records. But he said the possibility of abuse should not by itself prevent law enforcement from acquiring modern investigative capabilities.

“There have been instances in the past where police faced strict departmental scrutiny for casually accessing call logs,” Singh said. “However, denying an essential investigative mechanism simply because abuse is theoretically possible is not a balanced approach.”

Singh pointed to India and the United States as examples of countries where law enforcement agencies have interception powers subject to statutory restrictions and oversight mechanisms. He argued that Nepal could develop a similarly controlled system rather than leave investigators without tools needed to tackle sophisticated criminal networks.

The distinction between obtaining historical communications data and intercepting communications as they occur is central to the debate.

Call detail records can show information such as the numbers involved in a call, the time and duration of the communication and, depending on the available records, information about the cell tower used. Live interception, by contrast, would give investigators access to the content of communications as they take place.

That difference makes the proposed authority particularly sensitive from a privacy perspective.

Cyber law expert and advocate Baburam Aryal said any law allowing interception would need to specify precisely when and why it could be used.

“The law must explicitly define the exact conditions under which law enforcement can intercept communications and mandate that the specific criminal purpose be legally recorded,” Aryal said. “Granting such authority without transparent, enforceable parameters significantly increases the risk of institutional abuse.”

Police officials insist that they are not seeking unrestricted powers.

A high-ranking official at Police Headquarters said the proposed authority would be used only in targeted criminal investigations and would require judicial approval and independent oversight.

“We are asking for interception powers strictly for targeted criminal investigations, subject to explicit judicial approval and independent regulatory oversight mechanisms,” the official said.

For legal experts, however, the details of those safeguards will be as important as the power itself.

Kharel has proposed a two-tier system of protection. First, permission to intercept communications should come from an independent judicial authority outside the police, military and intelligence establishments. Second, the system should require public reporting after a specified period so that unlawful or politically motivated surveillance could eventually be exposed.

Such safeguards, he argued, would help prevent interception powers from becoming a tool for monitoring political opponents, journalists, activists or other citizens unrelated to criminal investigations.

The police proposal therefore presents the government with a difficult policy choice.

Law enforcement agencies want greater access to digital communications as crime becomes more technology-dependent.

Meanwhile, Nepal’s constitutional framework and judicial history impose significant limits on the state’s ability to intrude into private communications.

articles.title: Foreign medical students come to Nepal but twice as many Nepalis pursue medicine abroad
articles.summary:
Nepal is attracting a growing number of foreign students to its medical colleges, particularly for MBBS and postgraduate programmes, even as thousands of Nepali students continue to leave the country to study medicine.

Data from the Medical Education Commission show that a total of 1,859 foreign students enrolled in medical education programmes in Nepal between 2024 and 2026. During the same period, as many as 4,741 Nepali students obtained approval from the commission to pursue medical education abroad.

Arjun Dhakal, information officer at the commission, however said that the figure of students approved to go abroad should not be read as the actual number who left Nepal, because not everyone who receives approval necessarily travels abroad for study.

MBBS (bachelor of medicine and bachelor of surgery) accounts for the largest share of movement in both directions. In the three-year period, 1,766 foreign students enrolled in MBBS programmes in Nepal, rising from 572 in 2024 to 770 in 2026. The figures suggest that Nepal’s medical colleges are becoming more attractive to foreign students, but not enough to fill the seats reserved for them.

The contrast is especially clear in other health programmes. Foreign students have been allocated seats in BDS (bachelor of dental surgery), BNS (bachelor of nursing science), BSc Nursing, BAMS (bachelor of Ayurvedic medicine and surgery), BPH (bachelor of public health) and B Pharm, among others, but not a single foreign student enrolled in these programmes in 2026. Even Nepali students did not fully occupy seats in some of these courses.

India is both the largest source of foreign students coming to Nepal for medical education and the leading destination for Nepali students pursuing medical studies abroad, according to data from the commission.

Nearly half of the Nepali students who obtained permission to pursue medical education abroad—from undergraduate and postgraduate programmes to doctoral studies—went to India. Over the three-year period, 1,677 students received approval to study in India, including around 1,350 pursuing MBBS and nursing.

Dhakal attributed the high number partly to Nepal’s recognition of India’s National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), which makes it easier for Nepali students to seek admission to Indian medical institutions. The open border and relatively easy movement between the two countries are other factors, he said.

“India is more accessible because of the open border and the ease of travel between the two countries,” said Dhakal.

Bangladesh was the second-most popular destination. More than 450 Nepali students went there to study medical education during the three-year period. Australia, China, the Philippines, the United States and the United Kingdom followed, with more than 100 students going to each of these countries for medical studies.

Most of those going abroad enrolled in undergraduate programmes, although some received scholarships, Dhakal said. The number of Nepali students receiving approval to study abroad fluctuated over the three years. In 2024, 1,515 students obtained permission, compared with 1,815 in 2025 and 1,411 in 2026.

Overall, only 26.59 percent of the seats set aside for foreign students were filled, according to commission data. The Medical Education Act 2019 allows up to one-third of total seats in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education to be allocated to foreign students.

According to undergraduate enrolment data, enrolment increased by 34 percent between 2024 and 2026. In 2024, medical colleges had 7,606 seats, of which 6,343 were filled. The number of seats rose to 8,070 in 2025, with 7,196 students admitted. In 2026, a total of 8,550 students enrolled against 9,273 available seats.

Shreekrishna Giri, a former vice-chairperson and current member of the Medical Education Commission, said Nepal had considerable potential to attract foreign medical students and that their numbers were gradually increasing. However, he cautioned against compromising academic standards in the drive to expand enrolment.

At postgraduate level, enrolment rose by around 22 percent over the three-year period. In 2024, 1,467 students enrolled out of 1,724 available seats. The number of seats increased to 2,086 in 2025, when 1,750 students enrolled. In 2026, 1,789 students enrolled out of 2,056 seats.

Although both the number of seats and total enrolment have increased, medical colleges have continued to struggle to fill all the seats approved by the commission. According to the commission, between 700 and 1,200 undergraduate seats and roughly 250 to 325 postgraduate seats remained vacant in the three years.

A particularly large number of seats reserved for foreign students remain unfilled. In 2026, 2,428 undergraduate seats were allocated to foreign students, but only 476 were filled, leaving 1,952 vacant. Under the existing provision, seats left vacant by foreign students can be offered to Nepali students.

The Private Medical and Dental College Association has called for an increase in the quota for foreign students. The association submitted a memorandum to Health and Food Safety Minister Nisha Mehta on July 30, seeking an expansion of the seats allocated to foreign students.

Association president Dr Gyanendra Man Singh Karki said the government should increase the quota if it wants to attract more foreign students. He said Nepal could enrol large numbers of foreign students in MBBS programmes if the government introduced clear policies and programmes.

Karki said Nepal could attract a significant number of Indian students if the government took the initiative to reach an agreement with India. Sri Lanka and the Maldives could also be potential sources of students for MBBS and MD programmes, he said.

“The Nepal government has made no real effort to attract foreign students. The entrance examination and admission process here have also become cumbersome. If the process is made easier, we can bring in as many foreign students as we want,” said Karki. “Foreign students also bring foreign currency which contributes to the country’s economy.”

Stakeholders and medical education experts, however, say increasing the number of seats alone should not be the priority. They argue that Nepal must first ensure the quality of medical education and the adequacy of infrastructure.

Giri said the number of foreign students could increase significantly if Nepal secures recognition from the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME), which would strengthen the international credibility of its medical education.

“Nepal has already moved ahead with the process of obtaining recognition. A team from the federation has also visited Nepal and made suggestions for some improvements. If those recommendations are addressed, Nepal can obtain recognition,” said Giri. “Once that happens, the credibility of Nepal’s medical education will increase internationally, and foreign students will be more interested in coming here.”

Giri warned that increasing seats beyond established standards simply to attract foreign students could undermine quality. “Medical education directly affects the health of every citizen. We must ensure minimum standards. Medical education is different from other disciplines. We cannot run medical education merely to produce people who obtain a licence,” he said. “Quality cannot be compromised. Medical education should not be viewed only in terms of money.”

Medical college operators, meanwhile, argue that seat numbers should be increased gradually in line with the availability of infrastructure and compliance with prescribed standards.

Karki said the state should adopt a clear policy to attract foreign students while ensuring that the necessary legal and administrative procedures are in place. “By educating foreign students, Nepali students also receive scholarships equivalent to 10 percent of the seats,” said Karki.

Dr Rajendra Koju, a professor at Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences, said any increase in seats should be based on demonstrable improvements in quality. “If quality is improved continuously, the number of students will increase on its own. If we focus only on increasing numbers without paying attention to quality, our credibility will decline,” said Koju.

He said seat numbers could be adjusted after assessing the number of patients available for clinical training and the physical and academic infrastructure of medical colleges. “Whether seats should be increased or reduced is directly linked to quality. That must always be considered when making such decisions,” he said.

Dr Manoj Humagain, dean of the Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences, also said seat expansion should follow the fulfilment of infrastructure and other regulatory requirements. He said the relatively lower cost of MBBS education in Nepal compared with neighbouring countries had helped increase foreign students’ interest in Nepali medical colleges.

“Seats can be increased once the required infrastructure and standards are met. There is interest among foreign students. If their quota is increased, the scholarship quota for Nepali students can also be expanded,” said Humagain.

articles.title: Making power deliver
articles.summary:
On International Youth Day, Nepal needs more than another celebration of young people’s energy. It needs a practical question: Now that young citizens have altered the country’s politics, can we translate that renewal into wider economic opportunity and institutions that make power deliver?

The youth-led civic movement of September 2025 called for an accountable, responsive government. The election that followed turned that demand into a governing mandate. This was a political agency with national consequence. Yet, changing who holds authority is only the beginning; the larger task is improving what authority produces in everyday life.

This year’s International Youth Day theme, ‘Different Contexts, Common Aspirations’, speaks directly to Nepal. Young people broadly seek quality education, good health, dignified livelihoods, just treatment and a meaningful say in their future. Yet gender, caste, disability, geography, income and care responsibilities shape access to skills, finance, networks and voice.

The 2021 census counted 5.75 million Nepalis aged 15 to 24, nearly one in five people. Of these, 24.6 percent were not in employment, education or training, ranging from 36.7 percent in Madhesh to 17.5 percent in Bagmati. Policy for an imaginary ‘average’ young person will miss both. Inclusive delivery requires common pathways, support proportionate to barriers, and results showing who progresses and who remains excluded.

Agency carries responsibility

Young Nepalis have long contributed to democratic movements, community action, enterprise and civic innovation while seeking a greater voice in consequential decisions. The opportunity now is to turn generational change into better government—through genuine participation, accountable decisions and public action focused on results.

Formal authority comes with office; leadership is demonstrated through action. That work must extend beyond protest and elections into policy, implementation, enterprise and institution-building. This is not a choice between youth and experience. Nepal needs both working together.

Agency carries responsibility, but the burden cannot rest on young people alone. Those of us with authority or expertise must listen, open decision-making space and answer for whether institutions translate aspiration into opportunity. Young citizens have changed politics. The next test is what renewed politics delivers.

Economic opportunity is the test

The durability of political renewal will be decided in everyday economic life. Can education lead to work? Can an idea become an enterprise? Can a capable young person see a credible route to dignity and progress at home?

The Department of Foreign Employment issued 792,187 new and renewed labour approvals in fiscal year 2025/26. Migration has raised incomes, financed education and connected Nepal to the world; it is not simply failure. But choice matters. People should be able to go abroad by choice, not because effort and opportunity remain disconnected at home.

The World Bank estimates Nepal will need about 6.5 million jobs over three decades. No training, credit or start-up initiative can meet that scale alone. Nepal needs complete pathways: education to work experience; skills to employers; enterprises to capability, finance and markets; and local potential to wider opportunity.

The policy direction is clearer. The Sixteenth Plan, formulated by the National Planning Commission (NPC), puts productive employment, entrepreneurship and domestic opportunity at the centre of structural transformation. The government's National Commitment recognises the private sector as the main engine of job creation, with the government creating enabling conditions for investment and growth.

Action has begun. The Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies has adopted a Startup Fast Track action plan, while the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment has approved integrated Employment, Skills and Entrepreneurship Centres. The budget also introduces a National Apprenticeship Programme linking youth to employment-intensive industries through training and private-sector placement. The next task is disciplined implementation and measurable results.

The proposed National Enterprise Facility, led by the Industry Ministry with NPC support, follows the same catalytic logic. It reflects the government listening to startups and acting on policy commitments, particularly around startup capital and growth markets. By using public resources and authority to create an enabling environment and partnerships that multiply capability, finance and market access, the NEF demonstrates a Multiplier Nation: public action crowding in private investment, expertise, diaspora knowledge and local initiative.

Inputs and outputs matter—training, finance, centres and platforms must become operational. But they are milestones. We must also track outcomes—how many people move from learning to earning, how many viable enterprises gain finance and markets, and whether opportunity becomes easier to reach across Nepal.

Leading through uncertainty

Uncertainty operates at every level. Locally, climate shocks, migration and changing livelihoods are reshaping communities. Nationally, demographic change, fiscal pressures and evolving federal institutions are altering development choices. Globally, AI is transforming work, conflicts are disrupting energy and trade, and pandemics have exposed fragile labour and care systems. Aid and trade patterns are also shifting as Nepal approaches graduation from least developed country status.

The outcomes citizens seek remain straightforward; achieving them is not. Public challenges often involve competing interests, behaviour change and coordination across institutions. No expert begins with a complete answer. Leadership requires confidence to set direction and humility to learn during implementation.

We must prepare young people not only for today's jobs, but for problems without manuals. Technical, digital and entrepreneurial skills are essential. So are the capabilities to act with purpose, understand different lives, see systems rather than symptoms and collaborate across differences.

These capabilities shape technology's use. AI can multiply knowledge, speed and reach, but cannot choose which public problems matter, reconcile values or earn collective trust. Technology must remain a tool; human progress must remain the purpose.

Building institutions that deliver

Capable individuals cannot sustain transformation inside institutions that resist learning or rely on exceptional personalities. Individual brilliance is not a development strategy.

In 1972, Aaron Wildavsky published Why Planning Fails in Nepal. His enduring insight was that plans alone cannot create the conditions needed for their success. The constructive lesson today is that sound policy must be matched by institutions capable of learning, adapting and delivering.

The related risk is a capability trap—changing what an institution looks like without improving what it can do. Avoiding it means beginning with real public problems, learning through implementation and judging reform by better outcomes, not procedural completion.

This requires disciplined experimentation, early reporting of problems and operating systems that enable delivery—from recruitment and budgets to procurement, data and performance. Every reform should leave stronger people, processes and relationships. Otherwise, capability has been rented, not built.

The government's commitment to delivery-based governance creates room for this shift. Policy and budgets should respond to lessons from implementation, performance systems should track whether citizens see better results, and successful approaches should expand. National direction must remain clear; implementation should improve through evidence.

International Youth Day should mark a transition from celebrating potential to shared responsibility. Young Nepalis have advanced political renewal. Our task is to multiply economic opportunity, prepare a generation to lead through uncertainty and build institutions that make progress endure.

Political agency can open a new chapter. Economic opportunity will determine whether it lasts; adaptive leadership and capable institutions whether progress becomes cumulative. The unfinished task is not simply to assume power, but to make power deliver, and leave the next generation a state better able to serve.

articles.title: चक्कु प्रहारबाट मजदुरको मृत्यु
articles.summary:
बागलुङ काठेखोला गाउँपालिका–३ धम्जामा चक्कु प्रहारबाट एक मजदुर मृत्यु भएको छ।

जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालयका सूचना अधिकारी रामेश्वर त्वातीका अनुसार ढोरपाटन नगरपालिका–५ का २५ वर्षीय अर्जुन घर्तीले आपसी विवादमा चक्कु प्रहार गर्दा सोही नगरपालिका–७ का ४० वर्षीय अशोक खत्रीको घटनास्थलमै मृत्यु भएको हो।

हत्या अभियोगमा घर्तीलाई हिरासतमा लिइएको छ। घटना गए राति भएको हो।

हिरासतमा राखेर अनुसन्धान गर्ने अनुमतिका निम्ति निजलाई जिल्ला अदालत पुर्याइएको छ।

articles.title: विमलको निधनमा जनकपुरधाममा शोक बिदा
articles.summary:
वरिष्ठ साहित्यकार, भाषाविद् तथा शिक्षाविद् प्राध्यापक डा राजेन्द्र प्रसाद विमलको निधनप्रति शोक व्यक्त गर्दै जनकपुरधाम उपमहानगरपालिकाले बुधबार नगर क्षेत्रभित्रका सम्पूर्ण शैक्षिक संस्था बन्द गर्ने निर्णय गरेको छ।

उपमहानगरपालिकाले मंगलबार सूचना जारी गर्दै २०८३ साउन २७ गते बुधबार नगर क्षेत्रभित्र सञ्चालित सबै सामुदायिक तथा संस्थागत विद्यालयमा शोक मनाउँदै पठनपाठन बन्द गर्न अनुरोध गरेको हो।

सूचनामा डा विमलले शिक्षा, संस्कृति, पूर्वीय दर्शन तथा मैथिली र नेपाली साहित्यको क्षेत्रमा उल्लेखनीय योगदान पुर्‍याएको उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

डा विमलको निधनले समग्र जनकपुरधामवासी मर्माहत भएको जनाउँदै उपमहानगरपालिकाले उनको महाप्रस्थानले जनकपुरधामको साहित्यिक तथा बौद्धिक क्षेत्रमा अपूरणीय क्षति पुगेको जनाएको छ।
